data.title: M3: Kit v0
data.description:
Tests H4 (declare grammars as constructs and slots), H11 (Dialects own their passes), H5 (a fresh agent builds from about 8,000 tokens of docs) and H2 (three Dialects, one of each kind). The kit is extracted behind a generic Definition API, the existing Dialects are re-declared through it with identical output, a query and pass API is added, and a third Dialect (data tools with a SQL plugin) is built from Dream Code.

Plan and binding rulings: project/2026-11-24-m3-kit-v0-plan.md. The third Dialect's Dream Code: project/2026-11-24-data-tools-dream-code.md.

data.title: Design the Definition API from DMG, fields and the data-tools Dream Code
data.description:
Why: the proposal's §8.1 Dialect(...) sketch was never built; both existing Dialects are hand-written data plus hand-written builders. Everything else in M3 is shaped by this API, so it is designed from three data points before any of it is built.

What: a dated design doc under project/ (and a hand-written sketch of each of the three Dialects as Definition API calls, as pseudocode checked for expressiveness) that says: what a Dialect declares (types, number type, Iteration Spaces, intrinsics with each target's spelling and a reference implementation, a Library, targets with their compare mode, size flags, declared purity and effects); what a Grammar declares (constructs, slots of three kinds, fragments); how the generated builder reports errors; where a slot in another language (SQL) fits; and what from the M2 findings' "What M3 should change" is in or out. Settle the two decisions in it that the plan names (program DAG; foreign slots) or raise them for Ben.

Already decided: the tolerance rule (one declared figure plus a per-case override with a reason); Dialects are nominally typed; Dialects import by namespace with named interface types at the seam (the composition note's B-with-C, a recommendation, not built, so this leaf says whether v0 includes it); Dream Code before Dialect.

Seams: reads kit/dialects/dmg, kit/dialects/fields, kit/lower/environment.d.ts and the Dream Code. Writes only a doc. The doc compares every Environment field with its Definition API call and lists any field the API cannot express.

Out of scope: building any of it.

Open questions for Ben: the program DAG and foreign-slot decisions, if the evidence does not settle them.

criteria.label: Every field of the DMG and fields Environments is mapped to a Definition API declaration, or listed as not expressible, in the design doc
The data-tools Dream Code's ten examples are each placed against the API, with the gaps named
The two plan decisions (program DAG, foreign slots) are settled by Ben or carried as open leaves

data.title: Decision: is the program DAG part of the kit core?
data.description:
Question: the data-tools Dream Code has a DAG of tables, params, charts and views, with lineage and "what reruns when a param moves". The DMG's Game and a field's params are also structures above the Kernels. Should the kit own one generic graph IR, with the query API answering lineage questions over it, or should each Dialect keep its own structure?

Options: (a) a small generic graph IR in the kit, which Dialects instantiate; (b) per-Dialect structures, with the query API covering Kernels only; (c) a graph IR in the kit only when a second Dialect needs it.

What waits on it: the query and pass API's scope, and the data-tools Grammar. Needs the design leaf's evidence first.

data.title: Decision: how the SQL plugin runs
data.description:
Question: the Dream Code's SQL component needs a parser (for spans and schema inference), a checker, and an engine to run the query.

Options: (a) a hand-written SQL subset (select, join, where, group by, order by, limit, a few functions): no dependency, spans and schemas for free, real work, never SQLite; (b) an embedded engine such as sql.js (wasm): real SQL, a dependency and a large blob in a one-page artifact (check the M0 platform findings for what a page can fetch); (c) (a) for checking and inference, (b) for execution.

Project rule: avoid dependencies; ask before adding one. What waits on it: the data-tools Dialect's SQL slot.

data.title: The Definition API, Dialect half
data.description:
Why: the first half of H4. Two Dialects are hand-written data; the API must produce the same Environments, so that the lowering, interpreter, backends and harness need no change.

What: kit/define (or the name the design doc argues for): a Dialect definition function whose result is a Dialect value that yields the Environment (and the intrinsic tables the backends read) today's hand-written code produces: types and nominal vectors, the default number type, Iteration Spaces, intrinsics with each target's spelling and a reference implementation, a Library, size flags, and each target's compare mode. Declared purity and the loop-bound rule become declared properties rather than inferences. Diagnostics from a bad definition name the declaration and the fix.

Already decided: see the design doc and the plan's rulings. Tolerance moves to the GLSL target in the leaf that follows.

Seams: new kit directory; kit/lower/environment.d.ts must stay what lowering reads. Out of scope: constructs, slots and fragments (Grammar half), re-declaring DMG.

criteria.label: A Dialect defined through the API yields an Environment equal to the hand-written fields one (a test compares them structurally)
A bad definition is refused with a message naming the declaration and the fix, with tests

data.title: Re-declare the fields Dialect through the Definition API
data.description:
Why: fields is the smaller test of H4; it also carries the intrinsics, the Library and the GLSL spellings.

What: kit/dialects/fields is defined with the Dialect half. Its tests, the two survey sketches, the call-style sketches, the interpreter, JS and GLSL emission, the harness figures (JS equals the interpreter to the bit; GLSL within 2.19e-4 on a GPU; 28 planted faults, JS 24 of 26, GLSL 21 of 24) and the H3 trial kit are unchanged. Delete the hand-written data the definition replaces. Record every change to existing code in a note, for H4.

Out of scope: the Grammar half; DMG.

criteria.label: npm test and the prerelease suite pass with the fields Dialect defined through the API and no hand-written duplicate left
The harness figures and the planted-fault tally are unchanged, with the commands that reproduce them in a note

data.title: Targets declare their compare mode; the tolerance moves to the GLSL target
data.description:
Why: Ben ruled one declared figure plus a per-case override that names its reason (M2 findings, open ruling 1). Today `GLSL_TOLERANCE` lives in kit/harness/tolerance.js and the stress case reaches 5.2e-3.

What: the GLSL target declares `compare: tolerance(1e-3)`; the harness reads it from the target; a case may override it with a stated reason, and the harness output and `faultProblems` report an override. The stress case uses the override with its measured reason. JS keeps exact comparison.

Seams: kit/harness, kit/emit/glsl (or the Dialect's target declaration), scripts/shader-diff. Out of scope: changing the figure.

criteria.label: The harness reads the figure from the GLSL target, and no tolerance constant remains in kit/harness
An override without a reason is refused; one with a reason is printed in the report, with tests

data.title: Convert the data-tools Dream Code to a Dialect
data.description:
Why: the third data point, and the first Dialect with a row Iteration Space, string and date types and typed operators, effects and stores outside the DMG. H2 is only half tested until a data Dialect exists.

What: kit/dialects/data (Dialect half only): the `row` and group Iteration Spaces, column types from a schema (int, f64, string, date, bool), intrinsics for the Dream Code's functions, runtime lambdas (`derive`, `filter`) lowering against an Environment built per program from the tables' schemas, and typed errors that name both types and the fix. The SQL slot as the decision leaf settles. Write the Dream Code's examples as tests of the Dialect (those that need no Grammar).

Already decided: the Dream Code is the input and Ben's instruction is to convert it, then the Grammar eventually; the Dream Code's namespaces and codes were invented for illustration and may change.

Risks: strings and dates may need core types or operators the IR lacks (D1: typed operators already exist); the first effects that are not game state; record each change to the core in a note, for H2.

Out of scope: the Grammar half; the workbench UI (M4).

criteria.label: Runtime lambdas from the Dream Code's examples 2 to 5 lower and verify against a schema-built Environment, with tests
Every change to the core IR, lowering or backends is listed in a note, for the H2 count

data.title: The Definition API, Grammar half
data.description:
Why: the H4 test proper: "most fluent grammars can be declared as constructs and slots". DMG's Game and component, and fields' `field(...)`, are hand-written builders.

What: declare a Grammar: constructs and their slots (a declaration, a Build-time Lambda, a Runtime Lambda, and whatever slot kind the design doc gives a SQL body), fragments that add methods and typed attributes with conflict reports, and a generated builder whose misuse gives diagnostics with a code, a span, a "did you mean" and a fix (proxy objects where useful). The generated builder lowers each Runtime Lambda through the existing lowering.

Out of scope: re-declaring DMG and fields (next leaves); the book and IDE (M4).

criteria.label: A Grammar declared through the API generates a builder, with tests for a misspelled method, a missing slot and a fragment conflict
A build-time lambda that reads a param is refused with a message that names the fix

data.title: Re-declare the fields Grammar, then the DMG Dialect and Grammar
data.description:
Why: DMG is the real test of H4: the largest grammar, with stores, effects and integer rules. The bar is Ben's ruling: identical IR and output.

What: the fields Grammar, then the DMG Dialect and Grammar, are declared through the API. The M1 survey (126 lambdas, 111 lowered, 7 helpers, 4 subset, 4 not-yet), the IR goldens, the emit goldens, the 25-lambda swap diff (0 differences) and the planted-fault run are unchanged. Compare the generated builder with the hand-written one and record what a hand-written builder still had to add: that is H4's result.

Seams: kit/dialects/dmg, kit/dialects/fields. Do this as two commits, fields first. Record every change to existing code in a note.

criteria.label: The DMG survey, goldens, differential run and planted-fault run are unchanged, with the commands in a note
The result of H4 is written down, naming which parts of each grammar needed a hand-written builder and why

data.title: The data-tools Grammar
data.description:
Why: Ben's instruction is Dream Code, then Dialect, then the Grammar eventually. This is the Grammar: source, table, param, chart, sql and view as constructs; fragments; the Environment's mutation API as the agent's surface.

What: the Dream Code's examples run, as far as the Grammar and the Dialect carry them, through the generated builder. Charts and views are declarations and need no rendering here (M4).

Out of scope: rendering, skins and the book (M4).

criteria.label: Examples 1 to 5 and 7 of the Dream Code run through the generated builder, with tests

data.title: The query and pass API
data.description:
Why: H11, and the second thing M1 and M2 asked for. The IR records every statement's effects, so "who writes Mole.ttl?" and "what is the loop nest?" are cheap; the proposal promises only a JSON form. The data-tools Dream Code adds lineage and "what reruns when a param moves".

What: queries (loops, effects, def-use, reaching stores, whatever the program-DAG decision adds) and a pass manager in which a Dialect can add a pass above the core, each pass gated by the verifier and by the differential check. Include one real domain pass as the first test (for example, a pass that drops a store the DMG proves dead, or one data-tools lineage query), and a way to print what a pass did.

Already decided: the kit owns the core and its invariants, and Dialects add passes above it (proposal §5.1, corrected 2026-11-23). Range analysis stays parked unless a pass in this leaf needs it.

Open questions: how general the API is. Manuel's caution applies: too abstract defeats an agent asked a concrete question.

criteria.label: A pass written against the API changes a Kernel, is gated by the verifier and the differential check, and a pass that breaks the check is refused, with tests
Queries answer who writes a place and what a loop's body reads, on a DMG Kernel, with tests

data.title: Write START.md, API.md and hello
data.description:

data.description:
Question: the done-when is a fresh agent building a third workbench from the documents alone. The data-tools workbench is now in the repo, so an agent that can read it is not fresh.

Options: (a) rebuild data tools with the converted Dialect hidden from the agent; (b) a fourth domain the repo has not seen; (c) both, in separate runs.

data.title: Fresh-agent runs (H5, H11, H2)
data.description:
Why: the M3 done-when.

What: fresh agents given only START.md, API.md and `hello` (a) build a small workbench Dialect and Grammar with a SQL-like or other plugin and (b) write a domain pass against the query and pass API. Say how many agents and which model, since the subject is models.

Failure is information: if an agent had to read kit source, H5 or H11 fails, and the findings say what to move into the docs.

criteria.label: The runs are recorded with tokens read, iterations, files opened and errors by kind

data.description:

H2: every change M3 made to M1 and M2 code beyond the planned work (the leaves' notes record them), and whether the core stayed neutral across three Dialects. H5 and H11 from the fresh runs. criteria.label: The findings give H2, H4, H5 and H11 verdicts with reproducible figures
Earlier docs M3's findings overturn are corrected in place, as marked blocks

data.title: Decision: the capture policy for build-time values
data.description:
Question: real DSL code closes over build-time values (`row[column]`, `q[lo]`, `bucket`, `user`, `at`), as the Dream Code's fragments and `cohort` component do. The Runtime Subset rejects free variables and dynamic property names (proposal §5.5); M1 counted captures (11 of 126 DMG lambdas use a top-level helper) and rejected them with L001.

Options: (a) explicit build-time bindings: the construct passes named constants into the lambda's environment, and a reference to anything else stays L001; (b) specialization: a lambda is lowered after the build-time values are substituted as constants, so `row[column]` with a known `column` becomes a field access; (c) refuse closures and let authors write the column name literally, with a fixit.

Why it matters: it decides whether fragments like `winsorize` and components like `cohort` can have runtime lambdas at all, and so how expressive Grammars can be. The design leaf proposes; this leaf records Ben's choice. Evidence first: how many Dream Code lambdas need it (the design leaf counts).

data.title: The program record: declarations as a uniform node list in the kit core
data.description:
Why: proposal §5.2 puts "Declarations: generic nodes for whatever the dialect's grammar declares, each pointing at its kernels" in the core; it was never built. The kit carries three parallel hand-written versions (DMG's declarations and lambda slots, fields' Program, the signatures lowering returns). Addresses, the graph view, the agent's `ir()`, the generated language reference and the dependency query all need one uniform node list.

What: a small program record in the kit core: a list of nodes, each with an id, a construct kind, its declared data, a span, a phase (build or run) and the Kernels it owns, in a stable JSON form with a listing. A Dialect fills it in; the kit does not know what the kinds mean. Edges are not stored: the dependency query (the query leaf) derives them from Kernel effects on declared places plus edges a Dialect declares for its non-Kernel nodes. DMG, fields and the data Dialect are three clients.

Already decided: the reviewer's reading, adopted as the working direction: declaration table in the kit; edges derived; execution and reactivity (rerun on a param move, caching, frame loops) are a Dialect's, not the core's (proposal §5.3 and §9.1). Not a generic DAG: DMG's graph is cyclic and a field's is a star.

Seams: kit/ir (new record type and verifier rule), kit/lower. Existing DMG and fields output must not change. Out of scope: a typed dataflow layer between nodes (build it only if a Dialect needs kit-checked values flowing between nodes; see the composition note).

data.title: Kit boundary, check, and a generic differential harness
data.description:
Why: H5 says the agent should not need kit source, which is measurable only if its work lives outside kit/ against a public import surface. The proposal's §11 has a layout, a check loop (`node kit/check.js`, at most 40 lines, every diagnostic with a code and a fix) and budgets enforced by tests; the plan had none of them. A fresh agent's Dialect also needs a generic way to run its Kernels through the interpreter and the emitted JS on sample inputs; kit/harness today runs only fields Programs, and the same differential gate is what H11's passes need.

What: (1) a kit boundary: Dialects live outside kit/ (move the three), and kit exports one documented surface; (2) `check`: one command that loads a Dialect and its programs and prints every diagnostic with a code, a span and a fix, and runs the verifier; (3) a generic differential harness, a library that takes any Dialect's Kernels, inputs and targets and compares them (the fields harness becomes one client); (4) the budget tests the proposal describes, for the docs' token size.

Seams: kit/harness, kit/dialects/*, package layout. Risk: moving Dialects out of kit/ touches every import; do it in one commit with the type check as the gate.

data.title: Emit SQL from table pipelines (optional, late)
data.description:
Optional, late. Proposal §6 names SQL a target plugin: something a Dialect compiles to. If the data Dialect's table operators are in place, emit a SQL SELECT from a table pipeline, golden-tested, with no engine and no dependency, so the data domain has a second backend as fields has JS and GLSL.

Why: it is the cheap way to test "one source drives two outputs" over tables, and it matches the proposal's meaning. It is not needed for H2, H4, H5 or H11. Do it only if the earlier leaves leave time, or the fresh-agent runs need a second backend to exercise. Out of scope: running SQL, parsing SQL (Ben ruled it is not an input).

data.title: Queries over Kernels and the program record
data.description: Why: Manuel's advice was inspection APIs first, and read-only queries need no Definition API: who writes a place, what a loop's body reads, def-use, reaching stores, and one dependency query fed by Kernel effects on declared places plus edges a Dialect declares for non-Kernel nodes (so 'downstream of a param' and 'who reads param k' are one query). The kit already hand-rolls pieces: kit/emit/glsl/capabilities.js looks through helpers for purity, and the verifier collects effects. Their answers are the evidence the program-record decision rests on. What: a small query library over Kernels and the program record, with tests on DMG and fields Kernels. Out of scope: passes (the pass manager leaf).

data.text:
REVISION 2026-11-24, after an independent Fable design review and Ben's rulings (SQL is not an input language; Dream Code may be rejected with errors and fixits). The design doc must also settle or carry:
1. Build against DMG first: write a throwaway EXECUTABLE DMG definition that reproduces dmgEnvironment for one hard preset (10 or 14), checked by deep equality over its slot refs, because pseudocode is weak protection for keyed slots, emit, inferred methods, list.with and drawResult unions. Fields is the cheap confirmation, not the first.
2. Split the API into a static part (types, intrinsics, Library, targets) and a program-shaped part (constructs to Environment and program record). An Environment cannot exist without a Program's declarations, so a Dialect half and a Grammar half cut through DMG's index.js, which is mostly that derivation.
3. Lambda kinds are four, not three: declaration; build-time lambda (async, may read data such as schemas and samples, returns more grammar, not constants: proposal §5.4 needs a correction); runtime Kernel lambda; host-JS lambda re-run when a param moves (`.title(() => ...)`, the proposal's browser-only state). Say how the API names each.
4. The capture policy for build-time values is a decision (leaf cfUzUl); count how many Dream Code lambdas need it.
5. A Dialect declares its own effect verbs: EffectVerb in kit/ir/ir.d.ts is a closed union of DMG verbs (sfx, toast, hud, spawn, destroy, end, rng). The core is still game-shaped there.
6. An integer value type and null semantics: the core has neither (numberType is f32|f64). Decide whether the data Dialect gets them or rejects what it cannot type (count(), LIMIT, dropNulls, units: int). Integers are also what M5's hostless backend needs.
7. Lambdas as source strings (fields) or functions via String(fn) (DMG, the Dream Code): the generated builder must pick one.
8. Where the tolerance lives: declare it in the Dialect's target declaration (proposal §8.1), not in kit/emit/glsl.
9. Rename one of: the live-session 'Environment' in the Dream Code, and the glossary's Environment (what lowering resolves against).
10. State H2's failure condition now: fails if data-specific logic lands in kit/ir or kit/lower, or if DMG or fields output moves. Also state what fraction of the data Dialect's meaning the IR carries (groupBy, join, agg and sort are not Kernels).
11. Reject-with-fixit policy: the Dream Code's layout inside programs (contradicts G3), Vega-Lite encodings, agent permissions, a global fragment registry, pivot/describe/winsorize breadth, async data reads beyond schema and sample, and program-editing mutations (addStep, toProgram; those are the lab API, M4) are not kit features. Each gets a diagnostic with a fixit where an author could write them, or is simply out.
12. The Dream Code's builder operators the SQL rewrite invented (Builder gaps): year/date parts, join with {on, take}, sort("-col"), semiJoin, keepGroups. They are the data Dialect's, not the kit's.
13. Fragments scoped to a Dialect or program, not a global registry. Dialect imports (composition note) are OUT of v0.

REFRAMED 2026-11-24. The question 'is the program DAG in the core' bundled three things: (1) the declaration table: yes, in the kit (proposal §5.2 already promised it; leaf RJtpuF); (2) edges: derived from Kernel effects on declared places plus edges a Dialect declares for non-Kernel nodes, not stored, and not a DAG (DMG is cyclic, a field is a star); (3) execution and reactivity (rerun on param move, caching, frames): a Dialect's, not the core's. The design leaf and the query leaf (dynUhe) supply evidence; this leaf is Ben's confirmation. Evidence that would change the reading: toward less, if the three program records share nothing beyond id, kind and span (then the kit owns only a nodes()/edges() interface); toward more, if a second domain needs typed values flowing between nodes with kit-checked types (the composition note's gaps 2 and 3); toward a shared relational stage, if table operators must reach a second backend.

REVISION 2026-11-24. No SQL slot: SQL is not an input language (the Dream Code was rewritten in the builder; see its Builder gaps). Accept the data Dialect's pure runtime lambdas and its table operators. Be honest about H2: the Dream Code's lambdas are all pure, so this Dialect does NOT exercise effects or stores; it presses on an integer value type, null semantics and captured build-time values, and most of its meaning (groupBy, agg, join, sort) is not Kernels at all. The findings must say what fraction of the Dialect the IR carries. Dream Code that the kit does not build is rejected with a diagnostic and a fixit, or left out; record which.

criteria.label: The generated DMG builder runs the 22 preset sources unmodified and yields declarations and lambda slots deep-equal to the original's (declarationsOf and lambdaSlots in scripts/dmg-oracle), with the same diagnostics on planted misuses, since the survey and goldens alone never call the builder

12. The Dream Code's builder operators the SQL rewrite invented (Builder gaps): year/date parts, join with {on, take}, sort("-col"), semiJoin, keepGroups. They are the data Dialect's, not the kit's.
13. Fragments scoped to a Dialect or program, not a global registry. Dialect imports (composition note) are OUT of v0.

data.title: Dogfood trial 1: three fresh agents map the data-tools Dream Code onto the draft Definition API
data.description:
Why: Ben's ruling (2026-11-24, now an AGENTS.md rule): whenever an agent is asked to use something we made, a few fresh agents use it and report before the design is locked in. Here the thing is the Definition API's draft, and the task is mapping the data-tools Dream Code onto it. How hard the mapping is, is the feedback on the Dialect API. No need to build the API first.

What: from the design leaf's output, write (1) a strict rule set for the conversion, checkable by a program where possible (a checker script in scripts/ that loads a candidate Dialect and prints every violation with a code and a fix: required declarations present, no f64 mixing, every Dream Code lambda either lowers or is rejected with a diagnostic, every rejected feature has a stated reason), and (2) the draft API as documentation only (the design doc's API section plus a small worked example, the DMG or fields definition, written in the draft). Give each of 3 fresh agents (say which model; the subject is models) only the rules, the draft API and the Dream Code, and have each convert it to a Dialect (and Grammar as far as the draft allows) written against the draft. Then review each result by hand. Record, per agent: tokens read, what they had to guess, what they asked for that the draft lacks, where the rules misled them, what they refused to map and why, and how much massage the output needed to pass the checker.

Already decided: the data Dialect has no SQL slot (SQL is not an input language); the Dream Code is a probe, and what the kit will not build is rejected with a diagnostic and a fixit; lambdas of the data Dialect are pure, so it does not test effects.

What this changes: the findings go into the design doc as marked corrections, and the Definition API leaf builds the revised design, not the first draft. If the agents converge on a different shape than the draft, the draft changes; if they diverge, the API has too many ways to say one thing.

Out of scope: building the API; the fresh-agent runs from START.md, API.md and hello (a later leaf, on another domain).

data.title: Core nominal scalar (dates): a Dialect-declared named f64 that compares only with its own kind
data.description:
Why: Ben ruled (2026-11-24) that dates are a core scalar. All three trial-1 agents needed dates and used three incompatible workarounds (project/2026-11-24-definition-api-trial-1.md).

What: a nominal scalar any Dialect can declare (types: { date: scalar("f64", { note }) }, api-draft.md): stored as an f64, comparable (<, <=, ===, !==) only with its own kind, accepted by no arithmetic operator, emitted as a plain number. Recommended backing for the data Dialect's date: f64 milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC (exact to 2^53 ms, covers timestamps, matches Date.getTime()); the backing is Ben's to confirm. Dialect-neutral (no date logic in kit/ir or kit/lower), and counted as a core change for H2.

Seams: kit/ir types, kit/lower operators, kit/interp, kit/emit/js; kit/define accepts scalar(). Out of scope: date intrinsics (the data Dialect's), time zones.

data.title: Decide: may a constant call a pure helper? (the generated const convention forbids it)
data.description: DECISION for Ben. Found in iJtvVE (4a640f7): kit/define's generated const convention forbids every effect (as DMG's does), so a fields constant can no longer call a helper; the hand-written fields Dialect allowed it. Repro: lowerField(field("c").fn("g", "() => 2").const("K", "g()").pixel("(uv, u) => color(K, 0, 0)").build()) gives L004 "A const may not 'call g'". Options: (a) keep it (constants are plain expressions; helpers belong in fn); (b) let a Dialect's const convention allow calls to pure helpers (forbid stores and emits only), which restores fields' behavior and is still safe for DMG if DMG's helpers with effects stay refused. Recommendation: (b), declared per Dialect, since a pure call cannot change anything. Not blocking.

data.title: kit/define: a lambda in oneOf(ref, lambda) is dropped silently (function) or read as a ref (source text)
data.description: Found in dogfood trial 2 (agent B, 2026-11-24), confirmed by the integrator. data.text:
Blind-pass design written: project/2026-11-24-architecture-consult-design.md (criterion ITS).

Recommendation in brief:
- At workbench scale the complexity moves out of optimizers and linkers and into four places: capturing behavior, defining dialects, the seams between them, and legibility. Optimization becomes scheduling and caching inside each dialect.
- Keep JS DSLs, our own parser, one typed IR, our own emitters, no embedded engine. Change four things: (1) parse whole program files, not only String(fn), for exact closure capture and spans; (2) the core IR is for behavior (kernels) only, and structure stays per-dialect data with addresses; (3) runtime values in structure get no special form: build-time param reads are plain values, tracked and rebuilt on change, and only cross-part signals need a kernel; (4) composition is a kit service: parts are processes with clocks, only signals (snapshots) and kernels cross, plus one lab: address scheme, a scheduler, and frame tags checked at crossings.
- Dialect = immutable builder classes + TS-like sig strings + slot markers (Build, Native, Kernel, GpuKernel) + engine + view + a required text(). Types flow because kernels are typed eagerly at the builder call.
- Worked example: Lantern Cave (cave + arcade + fields + tables), 61 lines, ~0.9–1.2k tokens.
- Top risks: capture rules versus natural code; one-pass dialect authoring from the docs alone; composition semantics. Each has a 0.5–2 day experiment in §7.
- Correction to the brief §6: Jig's L0–L6 are views computed from one compile, not successive lowerings.

I've written `design.md` beside the brief. It's about 9,800 words, longer than the 20-minute target (more like 25 minutes, much of it tables), with depth in appendices. Facts are tagged by how I know them: read in code, measured with a script over `inputs/`, or inferred. I ran nothing from Jig.

## Summary of the recommendation

Keep programs in JavaScript, but split them by when code runs. Code that runs once at build time stays ordinary JS, run natively, and the fluent builders record a graph of domain nodes. Any lambda that re-runs (on a parameter change, every tick) or runs per element (per cell, pixel or row) is written in **Kernel JS**: a strict subset of JS syntax with the kit's meaning. In Kernel JS, vector operators work, units and frames are type-checked, and `u8` state fields wrap.

The kit reads these lambdas with `String(fn)` and parses them. It looks up their free names among the module's top-level bindings, so helpers and constants just work, which is the one real advantage tracing has. It keeps natural operators and real `if`/loops, which tracing loses.

Kernel JS lowers into one small typed core for **behavior** only. A kit-owned reference interpreter fixes its meaning; it compiles to JS closures by default, GLSL/WGSL per pixel, and C for export. **Structure** goes into a graph typed by each DSL's schema, not into that core.

DSLs compose through typed ports. What crosses a port is one of about a dozen shared **seam types** (grid, mesh, signal, field and so on), each carrying unit, frame, identity space and clock. Code can cross too: one helper runs in JS at build time in one DSL and in GLSL in another, which ends the hand-duplicated shaders.

To define a DSL, a model writes a schema (about 700 tokens for a game DSL like DMG's), plus a reference runtime and views (I estimate 6–12k tokens). The kit derives the builder, checker, reference, completions, parameter panel and agent help from the schema. The worked example in the doc is a procedurally generated cave, played in a tile-game DSL and lit by a GPU lighting DSL, with seam errors shown in full.

## Old world vs new world

Keep the old world's semantics machinery and drop its machinery for scale and speed:

- **Carries over:** a typed core, staging (binding times), one IR read many ways, names as identity with provenance, dialects defined as data, legality per target, differential testing.
- **Dead weight:** SSA/CFG optimizers, separate compilation, incremental invalidation, lossless syntax trees, rich type systems.
- **New:** a language definition small enough for a model to write in one go, seams that are about meaning (millimetres vs metres, per frame vs per pixel), and tokens-to-correct as the cost to minimize.

Your suspicion holds but misses its upstream half. All three systems I read fail at the same spot: getting hold of runtime lambdas. Binding time is the concept that unifies seams, staging and "runtime values inside structure".

## Three biggest risks

Each has a one-to-two-day experiment in the doc, with a kill criterion.

1. **Kernel JS friction.** Models may keep writing outside the subset. On the evidence so far, a scan of DMG's 113 runtime lambdas found about four in five already inside it, and about one in ten reaching top-level helpers or constants.
2. **The schema layer costs more than it saves**, or forces real domains into `t.any` escape hatches.
3. **Seam types buy no real leverage** once DSLs are actually composed.

## Questions for you

1. Will DSL runtimes stay model-written per workbench, or come from a kit library of reusable runtimes?
2. Is composition within one workbench, or across workbenches by importing a published DSL?
3. Is C export a requirement or a demo?
4. What edit-to-run latency do you want? I assumed under 100 ms, excluding heavy domain compute.
5. When the DSL changes, should old programs be migrated, or just re-checked with presets as the regression suite?
6. Which small models, and do they have tool use?
7. Is checkJs meant to check programs, or only the kit's own code?
8. Do you have an evaluation yardstick the experiments should use?

## Where I think the brief is wrong

- **§1's list of hard problems leaves out getting hold of behavior and binding time.** Both come before seams, legibility and verification.
- **"One small typed core IR" is right for behavior and wrong for structure.** Forcing tile maps, B-rep timelines or tables into it would distort them.
- **`String(fn)` alone drops the values a lambda closes over.** Jig's cache key has exactly this gap: `hash.js` keys functions by `fn.toString()`.
- **G-verify overpromises.** We can show the fast backends agree with the reference interpreters. We can't show a model-written reference runtime means what the user intended.
- **checkJs as the checker for programs conflicts with C-browser**, because the TypeScript compiler is several MB to run in the page. It's fine for the kit's own code.
- **"The DSLs are JavaScript" needs a qualifier:** code that runs later or per element should be Kernel JS.
- **Two chapters of *Uncommon Math* are shorter than 94k characters** (34,884 and 57,034). The book's other figures check out.

I couldn't verify in an artifact whether `new Function` survives the CSP, or whether WebGPU is available. DMG and Jig both use `new Function`, and each is a 10-minute probe.

Jig is cloned in `jig/`. My scratch copies of the example files are in `../consult-scratch/`.

data.text: datadial: built in kit/lower/nullcheck.js (tests kit/lower/test/null-check.test.js). Loose `x != null` / `x == null` (and `undefined`) lower to present / not(present) and narrow any optional. Strict `x !== null` / `=== null` keep lowering to ne/eq against null (JS-exact) and narrow an optional primitive (number, nominal scalar, str, enum, bool) only. DEVIATION from the ruling: strict `x !== undefined` / `=== undefined` are refused (L003, fixit: compare with null), not narrowed. Why: emitted JS must mean what the source means (kit/emit/js/test/semantics.test.js pins `find` giving undefined and `m === null` being false for it). The IR has one empty value, null, so `x !== undefined` is true for an empty x in JS; narrowing on it, or lowering it to present, would be unsound or would change its meaning. Likewise strict `!== null` does not narrow a reference, since find gives undefined. Backend/IR changes: verifier's `present` takes any optional (was: entity refs only); JS emitter spells present `(x != null)` (was `!!x`, false for 0).

data.title: Null-check and constant-call fixes from the review of 62bec66
data.description:
Found by review of 62bec66 (rev-data, 2026-11-24). Probes: local/rev-data-probes/.
1 (important, regression) `x !== null` narrowing is unsound: the core itself yields undefined for primitives (find over numbers, kit/lower/query.js:48; indexing past a known length, kit/ir/types.js:167; optional struct key by destructuring, kit/lower/pattern.js:94). `const x = ns.find(n => n > 5); if (x !== null) return x + 1;` lowers clean and returns NaN. Before 62bec66 these were L003. Probe narrow-undef.test.js. The "trust the Dialect" premise in kit/lower/README.md, nullcheck.js, api-draft.md and data README is wrong and must be corrected as such.
2 (important, regression) A constant calling a helper is typed unknown (lowerConstants, kit/lower/index.js:182-198, lowers with noSignatures before helper inference), so type errors pass: fields const K = g() with g returning vec3 used as a scalar is accepted. Probes fields-const.test.js, const-types.test.js. The test "a fields constant may call a pure helper again" passes for the wrong reason.
3 (important) Same root: helper calls in constants are invisible to inference: a chain g -> h from a const throws TypeError (kit/ir/types.js:63 via call.js:198); const K = h(0.25) gives L014 on h; const J = g(); const K = J + 1 is L003 f32/f64.
4 (nit) README/dialect.js claim "the helper's own effects are judged by the same rule" is not enforced; true only because a generated Dialect has no effects but call. Say so.
7 (nits) kit/ir/ir.d.ts:125 present doc stale; `a === undefined` on a non-optional says "with null"; the L003 tip recommends x != null, which S116 warns about.

data.title: Module-scope review fixes: closures, bake, top-level scan, epilogue
data.description:
Found by review of 613926f (rev-scope, 2026-11-24). Probes: local/rev-scope-probes/.
1 (high) A factory-made arrow resolves its free names against the module scope: const k = 10; const mk = (k) => (x) => x * k; const triple = mk(3); a lambda calling triple compiles x * 10 (runtime x * 3), no diagnostic. String(fn) loses the closure; scope is consulted before buildTime. Fix: accept a scope arrow as a helper only when String(fn) equals its top-level declaration's initializer text (the host has it from topLevelBindings), else refuse. closure.probe.js.
2 (medium) bake uses Object.entries: sparse arrays shift indices, array extra props baked as items, getters invoked (twice: check and build can disagree), Array subclasses accepted, non-enumerable/Symbol keys dropped (bake(Math) is {}). Walk 0..length with own data properties only, getOwnPropertyDescriptors, refuse accessors/non-enumerable/Symbol keys, require Array.prototype; README: a Proxy cannot be detected. bake.probe.js, scope.probe.js.
3 (low-medium) topLevelNames misses names after a regex literal holding a quote, a second declaration on one line, ...rest, indented top-level declarations; wrongly lists destructuring-default names (Math) and nested column-0 declarations, giving false B008/B013 or losing B008's "use sin" tip. kit/parse/README.md overclaims. toplevel.probe.js, math.probe.js.
4 (low) The checker's epilogue local `o` shadows a top-level `o` (hooks.js withScope). epilogue.probe.js.
6 (nit) B012 on a builder reads "it holds a Object".
Note for Ben (not a bug): B002 also refuses top-level names that clash with the Program's own .fn/.const, beyond the ruling's Dialect/Library names.

data.description:
Found by review of c7ed99f (rev-bind, 2026-11-24). Probes (asserting): local/rev-bind-probes/.
M1 (medium) A valid top-level helper is refused as B012 "made by other code" when its declaration has a trailing comment without `;`, a leading comment, or wrapping parens: topLevelBindings' init is sliced from raw code to d.to (kit/parse/toplevel.js) and unitOf requires String(fn) === source (kit/define/scope.js:88). End init at the last non-blank char of the blanked text; strip balanced outer parens and leading comments. module-scope.test.js's top() builds sources from String(v) (a tautology): add a test that the scanner's init agrees with String(fn). helpers.probe.js.
L1 The recording $ has only a get trap: `in`, spread, Object.keys/entries, JSON.stringify see nothing and record nothing; a param named like a PROBE (inspect, constructor, valueOf, prototype, then) reads undefined silently; "t" in u is false, not B014. Add has/ownKeys/getOwnPropertyDescriptor traps that throw BuildError; refuse PROBE param names. params.probe.js.
L2 Host values are type-checked only when read at build time (README overclaims); out-of-range and NaN accepted; record.params keeps the declared value, not the host's; an unknown values key goes unreported when programFn throws a BuildError. values.probe.js.
L3 A `let` helper reassigned to a same-text factory arrow passes the guard: accept helpers only from const declarations. letreassign.probe.js.
L4 C001 accepts any function as default export (`() => program(...)`), rules.md says ($) => program(...). Decide: tighten or reword.
L5 Wording: early-read-late-use attributed to the next call ("read by t.filter#0"); a run-time-only member read before the root opens gives B003 with a tip leading to F002; params.js doc example stale.

data.title: kit/parse/toplevel: a regex after ')' is read as division, so a function body's const is listed as top-level and a closure becomes a helper
data.description: regexMayStart (toplevel.js:82-91) reads '/' after ')' as division, e.g. 'if (k) /\}/.test(s)'; topLevelKeywords keeps one depth counter for all bracket kinds, so an unbalanced closer inside the regex drops depth to 0 and inner consts are listed. helperSources (checker/examples.js:83) keeps the last of two same-named entries, so 'const k=100; const f0=mk(3); function mk(k){ if (k) /\}/.test(""); const f0=(x)=>x*k; return f0; }' builds f0 as '(x) => x * k' reading k=100, silently. Fix the lexer (track what each ')' closes; separate counters per bracket kind) AND refuse a duplicate top-level name as proof of a misread. data.title: Module-scope scan: line terminators, regex/template flips and quadratic time (review of c189880)
data.description:
Why: the module-scope scan (kit/parse/blank.js, toplevel.js) is what a Definition API host uses to vouch for a top-level helper (B012). A misread can make a closure pass as a helper that reads the wrong binding, silently: the one outcome that must never happen. Three review rounds running (04567fb, c2845ca, c189880) found a high bug of this kind. Review of c189880 by reviewer-scan, 2026-11-24; probes in local/rev-c189880-probes/ (lineterm, label, lexer, perf, fuzz.mjs, fuzz-guard.mjs, corpus.mjs).

Findings, all confirmed by probe:
1. HIGH: a line comment, a regex and an unclosed string end only at \n, not \r, U+2028 or U+2029, so code after one is hidden from the scan. An end-to-end probe builds a helper whose lowered body reads top-level k = 100 while the real function multiplies by 3. Nothing reports it.
2. HIGH as a class: any wrong regex-vs-division guess whose misread span holds a backtick flips template text and code for the rest of the file, so a declaration inside a template looks top-level and the real one disappears. ScanError fires only on a duplicate. Confirmed: a label after a statement with no ';' or after `if (a)` (c189880's label fix is incomplete). Also misread: `export default /re/`, `extends /re/`, `1./2`, `++/re/.lastIndex`. A balance guard (a closer that closes nothing, brackets open at EOF, odd backticks) catches both end-to-end probes and refuses none of 518 corpus files, but the fuzzer found one case where two flips cancel out.
3. MEDIUM: toplevel.js is quadratic. declaration() calls lineEnds at each newline and re-slices the text per whitespace character: 20k newlines in a comment inside a declaration take 6.1 s, 80k take 102 s.
4. LOW: `const f = (x) => x` followed by a line starting `{` runs init into the block, so B012 refuses a valid helper (fails safe).

The README's "known misreads" are not harmless: each is a way to a wrong helper. The TypeScript-parser oracle (local/rev-c2845ca-probes/oracle.mjs) should become a kept test either way: corpus plus cases in the fast suite, a seeded fuzz in prerelease asserting never a fake top-level name and never a wrong const init.

Decision for Ben: keep patching the hand lexer (fix 1, the keyword and label gaps, add the balance guard and the oracle tests), or replace blank.js and toplevel.js with a real JavaScript parser (acorn: about 120 KB, MIT, no dependencies, runs in the page; a new dependency, which needs Ben's approval).

criteria.label: The end-to-end probes in local/rev-c189880-probes (lineterm, label) refuse or read correctly, as kept tests
The TypeScript-parser oracle runs over the corpus in the fast suite and as a seeded fuzz in prerelease
perf.probe.js's inputs scan in linear time

data.title: kit/define: the review lows on within, bounds and required (aa80fb3)
data.description:
Why: the review of aa80fb3 (reviewer-within, 2026-11-24) found nothing serious, and seven lows on one surface. Probes in local/rev-aa80fb3-probes/ (within, bounds, required, nested-name, lower-ids .probe.js; run with node <path> from the repo root).

What, each confirmed by probe:
1. An opening name scoped within its own construct (account opens name("account", { within: "account" })) is accepted, and its uniqueness is never checked: each instance is its own scope. Make it D011 (within.probe.js case 4).
2. data("number", { min: 0 }) accepts Infinity, and { max: 10 } accepts -Infinity. Ruling (main thread, 2026-11-24): a bounded number is finite, as host param values already must be; refuse with B004.
3. A bound set no value can satisfy (min 0.5, max 0.6, whole) is accepted; only min > max is D011. Make an empty whole range D011 too.
4. required: false on the root gives D011 saying "is required but has no parent"; fix the message.
5. an() picks the article by first letter only ("an user", "an unit", "an one"). A small rule for the common cases is enough.
6. Doc gap that bites the stateful run: a stateful construct cannot reuse a scoped name across instances (the state namespace stays Program-wide, so stateOf could not tell them apart; within.probe.js case 5a). Say so in API.md's within sentence.
7. Doc gap: kit/define/README.md's "Ref ids" paragraph names two ways two instances share a name; within adds a third (handled by the ~2 guard; lower-ids.probe.js).

Seams: kit/define/validate-grammar.js, shapes.js, codes.js, README.md, kit/API.md (keep it short).

data.text: sheet-writer: drafted scripts/particles/docs/dream-code.md (worktree agent-ae881bcef69a5fd35) with 20 refusals, plus scripts/particles/README.md. Choices stated in the sheet: no spawn verb in lambdas (emitters are the only source); spawn may not kill; rng only directly in spawn; force writes vel only; no lambda writes age; whole-field writes only (p.vel.x = 0 refused); helpers are pure. Not yet through its blind readers.

REVISED 2026-11-24 (main thread, from Ben's question on system, network and graphics calls): the draft must also cover effects on intrinsics. Today every intrinsic is assumed pure ("no member can carry an effect", kit/define/README.md), so once slots allow effects, a Dialect could declare an I/O intrinsic and a pure slot could call it unseen. Draft: an intrinsic declares its effect kinds (none means pure); lowering adds them to the call's effects, as a method call's already include its callee's; each slot's allowed effects gate intrinsic calls too. Async never enters a lambda: network and long-running calls are request values the host runs (both app-DSL designs converge on this), so a request builder is pure. API.md must say plainly that the Dialect author vouches for each intrinsic's declared effects, since the kit cannot inspect a ref. Also from the app-DSL probe: shared state needs a fourth category beside pure, own-instance and commutative/run-once, a per-key ordered log (an outbox); say whether the draft includes it or parks it.

REVISED 2026-11-24 (from Ben's question "if the DSL has .play('song.mid'), who writes play so we can generate wasm or C?"): today an intrinsic's spelling is a per-target code template and there is no host interface, so a retargeted effectful intrinsic means hand-written glue per Dialect per target. Proposal for the draft, to confirm with Ben: an effectful intrinsic is a declared host import (name, type, effect kinds); its spelling on every target is "call import <name>". From the declared imports the kit generates the C header, the wasm import table, the JS host interface (.d.ts) and a recording stub for the reference interpreter, so the differential harness compares the sequence of host calls across targets without real I/O. The platform host library (WebAudio, SDL, the DMG runtime) stays hand-written by whoever builds that host. A build-time builder method (.music("song.mid")) is a fact in the Program record that the host reads, with no codegen. Particles needs almost none of this; settle the shape in the draft anyway. See project/2026-11-24-app-dsl-probe.md: both app designs describe host calls as data.

RULED 2026-11-24 (Ben): agents define host implementations somewhere, never handwaved, and may do it either way. (1) Net-new host code in the kit's own language (the glossary's Runtime Subset; a short name is pending, Ben's call), lowered, checked against its declared effects and portable to every backend: the Library grown from helpers into host modules. (2) A foreign module, a packaged JS file with a declared interface (names, types, effect kinds), trusted rather than lowered, accepted only by targets that can host it (JS; wasm in the page via imports; never GLSL; not C). Main-thread proposal for the draft: an import has an implementation per target, a Runtime Subset one counting for all; a Program using an import with no implementation for a target gets a capability refusal naming it. The reference interpreter calls a foreign JS module directly, so the differential harness still compares JS and wasm. Precedent: local/form-skate-workbench.html's Form.plugin (install($, ir) declares systems with .phase, .reads(places), .writes(places), .tick; createWorld returns the one host object that owns shared state; a Program composes plugins with $.use). Its World is arbitrary JS, hence JS-only: the gap this ruling closes. Backlog candidate: an embedded JS engine (QuickJS) so C can host a foreign module.

data.title: api-pilot scorer: wrong-reason rejects, one crash zeroes a run, forged results, timeout overflow
data.description:
Why: the api-pilot scorer decides the H5 run's headline; a fresh review of 6e4f3a7/697e208 (2026-11-25) found it can count a wrong-reason refusal as a correct reject and can zero a whole run for one program's crash. Probes: local/rev-scorer-probes/scorer.probe.js (modes misnamed, forge, bigtimeout).

What:
1. HIGH. A reject that failed with C001 or LOAD (the candidate's file didn't load, e.g. the grammar export misnamed) counts as correctly rejected (programs.js summarize; worker.js pass = codes.length > 0). Probe `misnamed`: reject 21/21 with every export missing. Fix: C001/LOAD/C005 never count as a reject; and report a second tally, rejects refused with their declared code.
2. MEDIUM. One C005 thrown by candidate check code while checking one program sets definitions ok=false and fails all 33 programs (reportThrown attributes it to the grammar file). A crash triggered by one program should fail that program only.
3. MEDIUM/adversarial. score() trusts the worker's result file: a candidate that writes a forged result and exits 0 passes (probe `forge`). Parent must check the result's (kind, file) set equals listPrograms(hidden) and recompute tallies and pass from the codes.
4. LOW. --timeout above 2^31-1 ms overflows setTimeout to 1 ms and fails a correct candidate (probe `bigtimeout`). Refuse it (exit 2).
5. LOW. The worker runs with stdio ignored, so a scorer/checker crash shows only as NO_RESULT blamed on the candidate. Keep its stderr and show it.

data.description:
Why: Ben (2026-11-25): a package must carry everything that rides with a DSL, not only its Dialect and Grammar. Decide it before the package format (Uld5D0) is fixed.

What: decide what travels with a Dialect package beyond its definitions, and how each part is represented.
- Supporting code: e.g. the backing implementation of a builder method or a verb, written in the destination language (C, JS) or in Bench. Weigh against the backlog's Lean entry, which rules that a Dialect's run semantics be writable in Bench, with foreign code the exception.

Options to weigh (Ben): Woodcase with annotations; OpenUI-style syntax (openui.com) or similar; a UI DSL of our own built with the kit (dogfooding); or accepting Web Components as is.
Per the AGENTS.md dogfood ruling, a chosen representation gets fresh-agent use before it is frozen.

data.description:

- conditions: "bool" on defineDialect: a number (or any non-bool) as an if/ternary condition or an operand of ! && || is an L error. Off by default, so fields, data and DMG are unchanged.
- an operator option on vector(), e.g. vector(2, "f64", { multiply: "scalar" }): vector*vector and number/vector are L errors; default keeps today's componentwise behavior.

- a convention option body: "block": an expression body is an L error.
- one code per mistake: after a lambda's parameter-count error (L010), no follow-on L001 for the same parameter ((t, live, rng) => rng() gives one diagnostic).

data.description:
Why: review of 9dfb56b and 8ad7338 (reviewer-strict, 2026-11-25; probes in local/rev-strict-probes/).

What: (H1) buildTimeShadows (kit/parse/toplevel.js:316) reuses belowTopLevel, which collects every arrow/function parameter in the file, so a top-level name that is also a top-level helper's or a Runtime Lambda's parameter is listed and a lambda reading the top-level name gets a false B013 (s1.js: const WIDTH beside a helper (r, WIDTH); s2.js: const dt beside a force (p, dt) and an update reading dt; shadows.probe.js: function area(r) beside const r; the export's own `$`). Count only build-time code's own bindings (the export body's locals and its nested functions/methods), not top-level helpers' or lambdas' parameters. (M1) the scan misses object-literal methods, class methods and arrow params after a parenthesized default ((a = f(1), K) =>) (shadow-miss.probe.js, hidden/accept/m1.js in the probes). (M2) returns on every path: a helper with `return 1` on one path and a bare `return;` on another is not refused (type f64?), so the error lands at a caller, or nowhere when uncalled under check: "all" (detail.probe.js A2, default-or.probe.js); case A gives two L003s. A helper that returns a value on some path must not also have a bare return. (L1) kit/lower/assign.js:67 still gives DMG's "keep changing state in an attribute" tip in every Dialect: move it behind Environment tips like the others; the neutral L007 size tip tells a Program author to declare a size, which only the Dialect author can do: reword. data.title: Shadow scan reads no parameters of a computed-, string- or numeric-keyed method, or one named of/new/if (fails open)
data.description: Verification of fcee599 (reviewer-kit-3, 2026-11-25), MEDIUM-LOW, fails open: kit/parse/toplevel.js buildCodeNames' method regex needs an identifier not in NOT_METHOD before '('. { ['build'](K) {…} }, { 'build'(K) {…} }, { 0(K) {…} }, { of(K) {…} }, { new(K) {…} }, { if(K) {…} } (and class forms) record no parameters, so a Runtime Lambda inside reading K gets the top-level K baked in. Fix idea: in object-literal/class-body position accept any property-name form before (…) {, or treat every (…) { that is not a statement head as binding its parameters. data.title: The run's state in defineDialect: state, checkState, text checked, U reserved
data.description:
Why: Ben ruled (2026-11-25) that the run's state shape is declared in the Dialect, not the UI, because the text view, headless runs, traces and M4's seams need it with no UI loaded. defineUI (next leaf) reads it. Plan and the calls made: project/2026-11-25-defineui-build-plan.md.

What: defineDialect takes an optional `state`: a plain object of member types in the Dialect's own type vocabulary ("f64", "bool", "str", declared vectors and scalars, enumOf, opt, struct, list(of, max)); a nested plain object is refused with a tip to write struct({…}). A malformed state is a new D code (empty state, a non-type, a bad list max), collected with every other problem as defineDialect does. The Dialect value gains the declared state, its resolved core Type, and checkState(value) listing every mismatch by path; when state is declared, the value's text checks its argument first and throws a clear error naming the paths. Without state, nothing changes.

Also: add U to the reserved letters (kit/define/codes.js RESERVED_LETTERS; kit/API.md "Your checks"), and rename the api-pilot reference grammar's own U001 to a free letter, keeping its scorer and records consistent.

Seams: kit/define (validate-dialect.js, dialect.js, types.js, codes.js, define.d.ts, README.md), kit/API.md and the topic pages that describe defineDialect's keys, kit/glossary.md if it defines State. Out of scope: defineUI itself; declaring state on fields or data (optional; data cannot).

data.title: defineUI in kit/define: the U checks, from the trial checker
data.description:
Why: a package's UI is one more call beside defineDialect and defineGrammar (Ben, 2026-11-25: it goes in kit/define). The trial (project/2026-11-25-ui-trial-findings.md) validated the draft with a checker in scripts/ui-trial/checker/; this builds those checks into the kit.

What: `defineUI(builder, decl)` exported from kit/define. It takes the package's Grammar builder and the declaration (stage, inputs, tiles, annotate; no state), checks everything, throws one DefinitionError with every U problem (path, message, tip, did-you-mean), and returns a frozen UI value. The codes are the packet's (scripts/ui-trial/docs/ui-draft.md, "Codes") with these changes: U006 retired (state lives in the Dialect); U013 also refuses a Dialect that declares no state; a `state` key is U001 with a tip pointing at defineDialect; stat takes `max?` (a number), a ruling. Paths and lambda reads resolve against the Dialect's state Type (a path stops at a list; a list has length and items; a vector's components). The checker's module-file checks (U008: a module that is a package file and defines its tag) need file text the kit cannot read: take what the trial checker's moduleText gave as an option, and say in the README what a host must pass.

Then make scripts/ui-trial/checker a thin consumer of the kit's defineUI, keep its CLI and test fixtures working with the state moved into each package's Dialect (maze, and the particles reference the fixtures use), and update its README. Recorded runs are history: do not rescore them.

Seams: new files under kit/define (keep each under ~400 lines), index.js, define.d.ts, codes.js (a UI_CODES table beside the others, every code exercised by a test), README.md. Out of scope: lowering UI lambdas (the next leaf), the agent-facing packet scripts/ui-trial/docs/ui-draft.md (the integrator updates it for the dogfood check), cross-package qualified ids beyond what the draft says (one package per page; a qualified id is U003).

data.title: Lower UI lambdas against a Program: types, L codes, results per key
data.description:
Why: the draft promises that UI value lambdas `(s, $) => …` (and a table column's `(row, s, $) => …`) are lowered like any lambda, so the UI reaches every backend and a type error is an L code; defineUI alone cannot type them because `$` depends on the Program's params, which the Dialect's environment(program) declares.

What: the UI value gets a lower step that takes one Program's record and lowers every UI lambda through kit/lower in an implied pure space, with `s` the Dialect's state Type, `$` from the Dialect's environment(program), a row the item Type of the table's list, and the result Type each key requires (badIf, expect: bool; value, y: a number; badge: str or null; tone: one of good warn bad dim; a stat's value a number or str). It returns the Kernels by id and the diagnostics, each tied to the tile and key it came from. Do not add a reserved slot-convention name to Dialects: build the conventions inside the UI's own environment wrapper.

Seams: kit/define (the UI files from the previous leaf, lower.js as the model), kit/lower only if a gap forces it (say so). Out of scope: a host that runs them; runs' headless runs (waits on f2dMku).
Risks: kit/lower may not type struct and list reads from a parameter the way UI lambdas need (s.bodies.length, row.speed); find out first and report before working around it.

A read through a local alias (const b = s.bounds; b.bogus), a local destructuring (const { bogus } = s.bounds), a conditional/logical/array/call root ((c ? s.a : s.b).bogus), a local shadowing a free name, or an unused destructured parameter passes U007 and the trial checker exits 0. README and UI_CODES claim reads resolve against the state Type. Fix: type locals (or refuse a local / non-identifier root holding a struct or list item); the lowering step (mkPzcU) types all of these once a Program is given, so weigh doing it there vs in defineUI. Probe: local/rev-ui1/lambda.probe.js (10 failing cases).

data.title: Scan rebuild residue: ?.keyword regex misread, RangeError escape, a README overstatement
data.description:
reviewer-scan-1 on 9117cbd (2026-11-25): nothing serious. Three small items, probes in local/rev-scan1/:
(1) LOW: acorn reads a `/` after `?.keyword` (`?.return`, `?.in`, `?.of`, `?.default`) as a regex. Across a line break, with a closing `/` later on that line, this hides a declaration from topLevelNames (hide.probe.mjs). Not realistically reachable. Cheap fix: a ScanError when a regexp token follows a keyword-named property after `?.`.
(2) LOW: a long operator chain (about 4,000 to 5,700 terms) parses but throws a raw RangeError from the analysis walk, not a ScanError, so withScope/define-trial would crash rather than report LOAD (deep4.probe.mjs). Fix: wrap analyze's walk and freenames' visit in the same RangeError-to-ScanError conversion.
(3) NOTE: the kit/parse README says the export's own parameter never counts in buildTimeShadows, but `export default (k) => { [1].map(x => x); return 1 }` lists k (toplevel.js:91-93); the old scan did the same (a spurious B013). Fix the README or exclude the export's params.

Seams relay trial: packet, runs and findings

data.text: Plan (main, 2026-11-25). Packet: scripts/seams-trial/{brief.md,run.sh,docs/} on main (seams.md is the agent-facing form of project/2026-11-25-seams-draft.md). Checker: C0nNGy (checker-seams-1, Opus, worktree seams-chk). Relays: each is three blind runs, maze and particles legs in parallel, then a compose leg on their hand-ins: run.sh maze|particles <dir> <model>; run.sh compose <dir> <model> <maze-leg> <particles-leg>. Proposed spread (Ben chose models last time; a two-way door, so integrator call): r1 all Sonnet, r2 all Haiku, r3 Opus authors + Sonnet composer. Field names and frames are deliberately not prescribed to the authors: whether strangers' ports meet unprompted is the main question (a record field mismatch has no fix in the draft, since glue lambdas are parked).

Progress: seam parser, frame graph, ports/frames/inputs stand-in (D024-D031) over the real kit/define, handles, compose stand-in, CLI built; maze+particles fixtures with ports check clean; compose fixture clean (wire level.out.picked -> fx.in.burst: at: maze.cell -> particles.px, point, x32 +[16,48]).
Findings so far: (1) draft's example diagnostic is labeled S202 but describes S251 (no frame path) - followed the table. (2) S202 'extra field' is strict: a maze Event with an extra field (kind) can never feed a particles burst without glue lambdas; composer is stuck. (3) extent [w,h] gives no origin: maze cell (0,0)=center of top-left cell, so 'fit' is half a cell off. (4) The draft does not say how an input's local type is named when the Dialect has several vector types of a dims; stand-in takes an optional 'type' key. (5) ref('in') can't be filled through kit names() (opens' refs are not checked there); stand-in injects the namespace into the Program (internals) and hides its own frames from callSite.

Done; handing back on wt/seams-chk (uncommitted). npm run typecheck clean; npm test 2232 pass, 7.6 s. Fixtures check clean for all three roles; one failing copy per D024-D031, S101-S301 (+S102, S257), G101-G113, G001-G006, C006, LOAD.
More findings: (6) kit/define lower.js checks a stateless construct's names() only against slot calls' refs, not the opening's (inst.calls excludes openCall) - looks like a kit bug. (7) G005 via hashes is bypassed by a composer who re-hashes. (8) A ref('in') B003 reads 'there is no in brust' - the namespace name 'in' reads badly in kit messages. (9) Event output from a lambda refused (D026): the draft allows a lambda for any output; chose path-only for Events.

data.title: Seams in kit/define: seam types, ports, frames, inputs and handles
data.description:
Why: a stranger's Dialect needs a way to declare what it offers and accepts, in a vocabulary every package shares. This is the first half of wwG0JR, and kit/compose (the next leaf) builds on it.

What: defineDialect accepts `ports` (out, in), `frames`, `edges` and `inputs` as the seams draft describes (project/2026-11-25-seams-draft.md, sections Seam types, Ports and Frames). It judges them with D codes at the Dialect's line. Every generated builder carries read-only `.out.<port>`, `.in.<port>` and `.frame.<name>` handles, built inside kit/define. The `in` namespace is filled from `ports.in` so that `ref("in")` checks a trigger by name. A built Program's output lambdas, extents and edges are lowered and checked when the Program lowers.

Already decided (the draft's rulings block, 2026-11-26): an Event output has no `from` (a runtime pushes it; refuse a `from` with a D code that says so); an Event input declares `delivery: "reliable"` (the default) or `{ keepLast: n }`; the kit's shared unit `s`, and rates per second only (`vec2@px/s`); `ref("in", { kind: "event" | "value" })`; Event records reach the lambda slots an input names, through a name it gives (the shape is your call: keep it consistent with how `inputs: { object, name }` and params are declared, and report it); output value lambdas may build a vector from scalar state. Points, vectors and quantities stay three kinds. Untagged numbers do not convert. Rotation, Grid, Image, Mesh, Field and Ids are not in v0.

Seams: port from scripts/seams-trial/checker/ (seam.js, ports.js, port-lower.js, handles.js, define.js; its README says what each does). Its D024–D031 are the starting codes: keep a code where its meaning is unchanged. The seam grammar may live in a new `kit/seam` module or inside kit/define, whichever keeps kit/define's files readable. kit/ must not import Node built-ins. Update kit/define/README.md, kit/API.md, kit/START.md where an agent building a Dialect needs it, and kit/glossary.md (Seam type, Port, Frame, Edge, Handle).

Out of scope: kit/compose and every S code that needs two parts (next leaf); the runtime, the scheduler and queue bounds (ZH4KWX).

Risks: the trial's stand-in reached into kit/define's Program object to fill the `in` namespace. Doing it properly may mean giving namespaces a real source in the Dialect. The UI value-lambda lowering may not build a vector from an array literal yet.

data.title: kit/compose: the glue program, frame paths, conversion plans, renames, cycles
data.description:
Why: the composer owns every fact that spans two parts. This module is where they are written and checked, and its composed record is what the scheduler (ZH4KWX) will run.

What: a new kit module, kit/compose, with `compose(name)`, `.part(builder)`, `.frame(a, b, edge | "fit")`, `.wire(out, in, options?)`, `.show(part)`, `.check()` and `.build()`, as the seams draft's "The glue program" section describes. It builds each part with its own Grammar, then builds the frame graph from each Dialect's edges and the glue's `.frame` calls. It judges each wire's seams field by field, plans each tagged field's conversion by kind (a point by scale and offset, a vector or rate by scale, a quantity by a uniform scale), and returns the composed record with every wire's plan as data. Every S diagnostic names both sides, as the draft's "Diagnostics that name both sides" section prints them.

Already decided (the draft's rulings block, 2026-11-26): wire options `{ rename: { from: to } }` (data only, each name checked against its side, with a did-you-mean) and `{ delay: true }`; a cycle of wires is an S error naming the loop unless one wire in it is delayed, and glue order never breaks one; each part keeps its own params and there is no glue-level `$`; one wire per input; no direct reads between parts; the composed record carries each wire's `convert`, `rename`, `delay`, dropped fields and the consumer's `delivery`. The page's composition is a root part in its own Dialect, so `.show(part)` stays a single part; no layering in kit/compose.

Seams: port from scripts/seams-trial/checker/ (compose.js, frames.js, glue-scan.js, codes.js). How a glue program's bare package names (`import { maze } from "maze"`) resolve goes through kit/package's loading (the trial's hooks stood in for it); read kit/package/README.md and reuse it rather than writing a second resolver. Write kit/compose/README.md (API, invariants, S codes) and add it to kit/API.md and kit/START.md.

Out of scope: running anything (ZH4KWX: the scheduler, delivery, queue-bound checks); the composed page's drawing (FqsPVJ).

Open: whether S301 (a handle used as a value at build time) can be trapped without scanning the glue's text. The trial scanned for conditions. Prefer a trap, and report what you chose.

data.text: From the 2026-11-26 rulings (project/2026-11-25-clocks-draft.md, rulings block): this leaf owns the Event queue-bound check at composition (tick→tick from the two rational periods and the producer's per-step max; demand consumers woken by the Event; frame consumers bounded by the catch-up cap), enforcing each input's `delivery` ("reliable" | { keepLast: n }) that kit/compose records, the capped catch-up loop that slows T instead of dropping Events, and R001 as the slowdown statistic. Blocked by wwG0JR because it runs kit/compose's composed record.

Ben, 2026-11-26: option (a), a draw list, "essentially draw calls which can then be lowered to GLSL, SDL, Canvas, or even Game Boy". Design notes for the draft: the draw list is target-neutral data in the part's frame, so a wire converts it and the root transforms and combines lists. Backends differ in how direct the lowering is: Canvas and SDL replay calls nearly one-to-one; GLSL needs a pass that turns primitives into geometry or instances (or an SDF evaluated per pixel); Game Boy has hard limits (a tile grid, 40 sprites with 10 per scanline, 4 shades), so a backend must declare what it can draw and the kit must refuse or report a list it cannot, rather than approximate silently. The primitive set should be small and designed against those limits from the start.

Chose to refuse rest() in opens at defineGrammar (D019 widened), not to record the tail. No Dialect in kit/dialects or any trial hand-in uses rest() in opens (grep for rest( across kit/dialects and scripts: every use is in a decl slot), so a variable-length opening has no user; refusing is the reversible option. Red test kit/define/test/opens-rest.test.js (D019 at constructs.chart.opens.2; rest(lambda()) still one D019; a slot's rest() still records every value). The probe's case A now throws D019 at defineGrammar. Docs: codes.js D019 text, kit/define/README.md, kit/API.md line on opt/rest.

- Q9 shape (my call, reversible): `record: { name, slots }` on an Event input. The kit makes a read-only object of the record's fields + a global `name`; each field read is the effect `read <name>.<field>` and only the listed slot conventions get `read <name>` in their may, so any other lambda's read is L004. Chosen over a trailing lambda parameter so the name is the Dialect's (the ruling says "the name it is read by"), and like params/inputs it is a global, but the kit declares the object and global itself (the author need not).
- A wrong-kind ref("in", { kind }) B003 lists the inputs of the right kind instead of a did-you-mean (an Event and a value input are rarely spelled alike).
- Output lambda building a vector: lowering types [a, b] as list(f64, 2), so port-lower pairs it with a point/vector seam only when the lambda body is an array literal of exactly the seam's dims.
Tests: kit/seam/test/{seam,frames}.test.js, kit/define/test/seams-{define,handles,lower}.test.js; define-trial check.test.js gains a fixture per new D code (its coverage test requires one). Docs: kit/define/README.md, API.md, START.md, glossary.md, kit/seam/README.md.

README.

Codes: the trial's S101-S114, S201-S204, S251-S257, S301 kept with their meanings; S201 widened to a rate into a non-rate. data.title: kit/compose: a handle tested as a condition is not S301 (the trial's glue scan was not ported)
data.description: Integrator's read of c513d92 (2026-11-26): kit/compose traps a handle read as a number or string (S301 through Symbol.toPrimitive, kit/define/handles.js), but a handle tested as a condition (`if (level.out.picked)`, `h ? a : b`, `!h`, `h && x`) is not caught: an object is always truthy, so the glue's branch silently always takes one side. The trial checker caught it by scanning the glue's text (scripts/seams-trial/checker/glue-scan.js in git history before c513d92); seams-build-1 ported the trap but not the scan. Fix: extend kit/compose's scanGlue (kit/compose/glue.js), which already parses the glue with kit/package's scan, to report S301 for a member chain ending in .out.X, .in.X or .frame.X in a test position, at its line. Red test first: each of the four forms above gives S301.

data.text: Ruled by Ben 2026-11-26: questions 1-5 as recommended (project/2026-11-26-build-record-draft.md, header). Build plan: the keys, revisions and build events as data are part of the runtime build (ZH4KWX), which needs revisions for inputs.$rev; the agent-facing `why` text gets the draft's small trial before it is fixed.

Ben, 2026-11-26: a handle is never a value at build time, so ANY test or comparison of one is S301, not only truthiness: `if (h)`, `h ? a : b`, `!h`, `h && x`, and also `h !== undefined`, `h === null`, `h != null` (always true for a handle, so they hide the same mistake). Arithmetic and ordering comparisons (`h > 0`) are already caught by the toPrimitive trap. Red tests for each form.

data.title: Bench: boolean-only conditions everywhere, the conditions option removed, every example rewritten
data.description:
Why: Ben, 2026-11-26: no truthiness in Bench. Today `conditions: "bool"` is an opt-in Dialect strictness option (kit/define README, "Strictness options"; kit/lower/expr.js ~501) and no Dialect declares it.

What: boolean-only conditions become the kit's only behavior. A non-bool if/ternary/loop test, or a non-bool operand of !, &&, || in a test, is L003, and the `conditions` option is removed (no opt-out; one way to write a condition). L003's tip writes the explicit form for the type found: optional `m === undefined`, number `n !== 0` (or `n > 0`), string `s !== ""`. kit/API.md pitfalls and kit/START.md say so.

Already decided: example workbenches are sketches, not oracles (Ben, 2026-11-26), so no Dialect-specific exception. DMG included.

DMG: measured 2026-11-26 (local/bool-dmg.probe.mjs, gitignored): 21 of the 111 preset lambdas that lower today fail under bool-only conditions, in 18 presets: an optional entity as a test (`if (!m) return` after w.rng.pick) or a number (`if (self.flap)`). Move the presets out of the archived HTML into a maintained file (scripts/dmg-oracle/presets.json; the loader reads it; project/2026-11-23-dmg-workbench.html stays as the dated record) and rewrite them there. Check each rewrite by running original and rewritten presets on the original runtime and comparing traces (scripts/dmg-diff); a deliberate behavior change re-baselines instead.

Also fix every other Program that breaks (fixtures, Dialect examples, recorded trial hand-ins), listing each edit, and record the count as a finding.
