runtime-build-1, start (worktree wt/runtime-build at 7ed9523).

Finding, brief vs repo: the letter R is NOT unused. kit/lir already reports R001-R006 (the shader backend's refusals: f64 precision, no LIR form, ...), and every particles package (scripts/seams-trial/fixtures/valid/particles, pkg-trial, the relay runs) uses R001-R010 as its own Dialect check codes, with a refusal manifest expecting R010. So the clocks draft's R001-R005 collide with kit/lir's codes, and reserving R in kit/define's RESERVED_LETTERS would break those packages. Reversible choice taken: run codes are R001-R006 as ruled, in kit/run's own codes table; R is not added to RESERVED_LETTERS. Needs Ben: rename one family, or accept per-module code spaces.

Plan: kit/define/runtime.js (defineRuntime, clockOf, rational times), kit/package entry.runtime, kit/build (content key with a sync sha256, revision rule, build events), kit/compose/queues.js (S116 queue bound, called by .check({ runtimes }) and by the scheduler), kit/run (scheduler, delivery, driver, replay, checkpoints). Acceptance in scripts/seams-trial/test/runtime.test.js on fixtures/valid with runtime modules.

Design call that changes what an author writes (reversible): an Event port's per-step max is declared in the runtime (events: { out: { picked: 8 }, in: { burst: 8 } }), since after the seams rulings an Event output has no from and so no state list max, and an Event seam has no max of its own.

data.title: kit/compose and kit/seam: six LOW review findings on c513d92
data.description:
reviewer-seams-2's six LOW findings on c513d92 (2026-11-26), each with a probe in /Users/ben/git/workbench/local/rev-seams-1/ (red tests):
1. A record field or frame named `__proto__` vanishes (plain {} objects): kit/seam/seam.js:61-71, kit/compose/wires.js:41, kit/define/ports.js:73. r2-proto.probe.mjs. Fix: Object.create(null), or refuse the name.
2. A port or frame named `then` makes reading its handle throw a TypeError (proxy invariant): kit/define/handles.js:77. r2-then-port.probe.mjs. Fix: refuse the name in ports.js (as D018 does for constructs), or check hasOwn first.
3. S115's named wire and its fix depend on .wire line order when two parallel wires close the loop, and the fix doesn't fix it (the parallel wire still closes the loop): kit/compose/wires.js:52-53, analyze.js:230. r2-cycle-order.probe.mjs. Fix: break ties by a stable key (port names), and name every undelayed wire between the two parts in the fix.
4. A false S113 (required input has no wire) when the glue wires it but the producer fails to build or names an unknown output: analyze.js:171-178. r2-broken-producer.probe.mjs.
5. S251 between f64@s and a package's own 1-dim frame suggests `.frame(a.frame.s, …)`, which is impossible (S111); say instead that the kit's s relates to no package frame: analyze.js:204-205. r2-sfix.probe.mjs.

data.title: kit/run and S116: the real-time driver exceeds the queue window S116 sizes (review of 04fc8f2)
data.description:
reviewer-run-1 on 04fc8f2 (2026-11-26), probes in /Users/ben/git/workbench/local/rev-run-1/ (red tests; kit.mjs is a shared helper). The real-time driver and S116's frame window:
H1 (HIGH): S116 passes a tick->frame wire, but under the driver the consumer takes more than its max in one step, silently. (a) The first frame takes the closed window [0, f1], one producer step more than S116 counts (the driver logs no frame at T = 0). (b) A merged short frame (driver.js:44 returns null, but `ideal` keeps the time) lets the next logged frame span cap + 1/240 s + ms rounding. s116-display-frame.probe.mjs cases 1-2; queues.js:78, driver.js:39-44. Nothing checks a step's intake against events.in (part.js:112-115 checks only out): add that run-time check as well (fail loud), and make the driver honor the window S116 assumes.
M1: the driver exceeds the window in other ways: pause then driver.step() then resume (s116-display-frame case 3; driver.js:30, scheduler.js:251); run.rewind does not reset the driver's `ideal`, so the next frame jumps T back uncapped with no R001 (rewind.probe.mjs case b); createDriver's catchUp is independent of the run's (driver-catchup-mismatch.probe.mjs; driver.js:18).
M4: S116 refuses a frame->frame wire that cannot overflow: stepsIn(frame, catchUp) counts a producer step every 1/240 s, but both step on the same frames (s116-overcount.probe.mjs lines 1-2; queues.js:27).
L1: a demand producer's steps are over-counted across coinciding tick clocks (s116-overcount line 3; queues.js:28-30).
L2: R001 is written only when an overload ends; a run that never recovers never reports (r001-open.probe.mjs; scheduler.js:178-184).
L4: a display frame's cost grows with run length (frameTs scans, unbounded hashes and inputs; driver-cost.probe.mjs; scheduler.js:141, :251).

data.title: kit/compose: S301 false positive on a logical's result operand; a handle's unknown property reads silently
data.description:
reviewer-compose-3 on e50172c (2026-11-26), probes in /Users/ben/git/workbench/local/rev-compose-3/ (shared helper tiny.mjs; run with node).

1. MEDIUM, a false S301 (scan2.probe.mjs). `const h = flag && level.out.picked`, `override || level.out.picked` and `override ?? level.out.picked` are refused, but the handle there is the result, not the tested value. glue.js tests both operands of a LogicalExpression. Fix: always test the left operand, and test the right operand only when the logical expression itself is in a test position (an if/while/for/?: test, the operand of `!`, or nested in such a logical). glue-scan.test.js's form `const x = 1 && level.out.picked;` must change to expect no S301, and the reason must be stated.
2. LOW, a silent miss (scan.probe.mjs). `if (a.out.x.y)` and `a.out?.x?.y` are not caught, because reading an unknown property of a handle gives undefined silently. Fix at the source: a handle (kit/define/handles.js) throws S301 on a read of any property it doesn't define (`then` and the symbols runtimes probe excepted; check what kit/compose and the trap themselves read), so the mistake fails loud however it was aliased.
3. LOW, docs. kit/compose/README.md must say the scan is by shape and misses aliases, destructuring and handles passed to helpers (`const h = a.out.x; if (h)`). It must also say an ordinary object with keys in/out/frame is flagged (`config.in.length`).
4. LOW. S301's line is the enclosing node's start line, not the handle's. Report the handle chain's own line.

data.title: kit/run: restart breaks chunked-run equality; replay tail; S116 demand→frame over-count; display runUntil window
data.description:
reviewer-run-2 on acc5434 (2026-11-26), probes in /Users/ben/git/workbench/local/rev-run-2/ (run with node). Each finding's probe is its red test.

1. HIGH, stopped-restart-chunks.probe.mjs. When a rebuild restarts the only clocked part (or a part whose init failed is fixed while every other part is demand), a chunked run and a one-go run differ, and instants run earlier than an input already applied. runUntil(3) gives 4 instants; runUntil(2) then runUntil(3) gives 8, at 1, 5/4, 3/2 and 7/4, after the rebuild stamped 2. A live run replays with N005. Trace in kit/run/scheduler.js: nextMultiple counts from lastT, not now. runUntil sets no `pinned` when `at` is null (`if (applyInputs(target, at) && at) pinned = at`), and its loop exits on nextInstant() === null without applying inputs.
2. MEDIUM, replay-tail-input.probe.mjs. Replay gives a false N005 for any run whose runUntil tail applied an input. replay.js:22-23 replays only to record.hashes.at(-1).T, so it never applies inputs the live run applied after its last instant.
3. MEDIUM, s116-demand-frame.probe.mjs. S116 refuses a demand producer into a frame consumer that cannot overflow (bound 16 at max 1; the largest batch seen is 1). queues.js stepsIn counts ceilDiv(span, MIN_FRAME) frames, but a frame consumer's window holds exactly one frame: 1 + tickInstants(…, catchUp).
4. LOW, display-rununtil.probe.mjs. runUntil on a display run, then a driver frame or step(), stops frame consumers with N002 and writes a misleading N001 (57.88×). driver.js limit() falls back to afterMs(run.T), but the cap still counts from the last logged frame. The README says the next frame counts from the run's T: make it so (e.g., runUntil on a display run logs a frame at its target, or the driver's window restarts at run.T).
5. LOW, pre-existing, frame-only-input.probe.mjs. In a display run of frame parts only, run.input() with the default stamp throws "not after the last instant run".
6. Tidy: three of local/rev-run-1's probes pass catchUp to createDriver, which now throws. Ported versions are port-rewind and port-s116-display-frame.

runtime-fix-2 (wt/runtime-fix-2), uncommitted: all six findings plus Ben's stopped-part ruling are fixed; every probe is ported as a test under kit/run/test/ (restart.test.js is new; the rest went into window.test.js) and each was seen red first.
Mechanisms. (1) While no part is due, inputs apply one stamp at a time, at their own stamps. A new `floor` makes nextMultiple and nextFrame count from that stamp, so a restarted part's first instant is the first on its clock at or after it. step() does the same. (2) record() now carries T (the T the run reached), and replay runs run.advance(T). An input stamped at or before run.T applies at once, as runUntil(run.T) would. (3) S116: a demand producer into a frame consumer counts 1 + tickInstants(cap). (4) runUntil on a display run with a running frame part logs frames up to its target: one a nominal frame after another, with the last two splitting what is left, and none closer than MIN_FRAME. run.advance and rewind log none. In a display run waiting on a frame that is not logged yet, tail inputs wait for that frame instead of pinning a tick ahead of it. (5) When no instant is due yet, the default stamp is run.T, or the first millisecond after it when run.T is the last instant run. (6) A stopped part's queues are cleared when it stops, and records sent to it while it is stopped are dropped. Both are counted in stats().stopped, with one N001 warning per wire.
Fuzzers on the branch: chunk-fuzz 300/0 failures, driver-fuzz 320/0, tick-instants 400/0. A driver-fuzz variant that adds runUntil ops plus a replay check after each one: 320/0.

data.text:
Ruled by Ben 2026-11-26 (session 3):
1. Kernels by name: as recommended. ctx.kernels["<instance>.<slot>.<name>"] for a named call; positional #n ids stay the stable id.
2. Per-Program state: a Dialect marks a state member extensible; a Program's declarations (e.g. .field) add typed fields to it, checked against the built record, like environment(program). N003 still holds; no cap.
3. $T: as recommended. The kit stamps each delivered Event record with its producer's T, read-only, beside $rev.
4. Optional input fields: as recommended. `name: type = default` on an Event input field, filled on the wire; a wire still never computes.
5. Controls: the page is a built-in part whose Event outputs are the controls, wired like any port (.wire(page.pad, maze.move)). Replaces polling ctx.controls by host convention.
6. A record global reads as null outside a record-driven call; lambdas test `burst != null` (fits boolean-only conditions: lowers to present).
7. S116 (new; Ben deferred to the recommendation): a wire may take { overflow: "keepLast" | "keepFirst" }; with a policy, S116 becomes a warning naming it, and drops are counted in stats() and noted once per wire (as for a stopped part). The consumer's max never changes. reference.md shows each Event port's max and delivery. Program-derived maxes go to the backlog until a trial needs them.

data.title: Runtime contract: kernels by name, $T on Event records, a record global that reads as null
data.description:
Why: the relay rerun's authors guessed and stalled at the runtime contract, not the seams (project/2026-11-26-seams-relay-rerun-findings.md, "Gaps"). Ben ruled 2026-11-26 (note on Vv3lQY; project/2026-11-26-runtime-contract-plan.md). This leaf builds the three rulings that change what a runtime and its lambdas are handed.

What: (1) ctx.kernels also keys each call that declares a name by "<instance>.<slot>.<name>"; the positional "<instance>.<slot>#<n>" id stays the stable id, and both reach the same kernel. (3) Every Event record delivered to a part carries a read-only $T, its producer's T at the instant it was sent, beside $rev; a runtime can't write it and replay reproduces it. (6) A record global (a Dialect port's `record: { name, slots }`) reads as null in a listed slot called without a record (a spawn by rate), instead of throwing; lambdas test `<name> != null`, which lowers to `present` under boolean-only conditions (kit/lower/README.md).

Seams: kit/run (scheduler.js after p4IYui's split, part.js, compile.js), kit/compose/queues.js for the stamp, kit/define/ports.js for the record's type (the global becomes optional). Docs: kit/run/README.md, kit/define/README.md, and the runtime section of kit/API.md; the docs use <placeholder> snippets, never worked examples (memory placeholders-not-examples).

Out of scope: per-Program state and input defaults (sibling rc-define); controls and overflow (rc-wire).

Risks: making the record global optional changes lowering for every listed slot, and existing lambdas that read it unguarded become L003. Survey the repo's packages and fixtures (scripts/seams-trial) and say what changed.

criteria.label: A test shows ctx.kernels["<instance>.<slot>.<name>"] and the positional id are the same kernel for a repeated named slot, and that an unnamed call has only the positional id.
A test shows a delivered record carries $T equal to the producer instant, that writing it throws or is refused, and that replay of a run that reads $T is clean.
A test shows a listed record slot called without a record sees null and that a lambda reading it without a null check is refused at lowering with a tip naming the check.
npm test and npm run typecheck pass; kit/run/README.md and kit/API.md say all three.

data.title: Runtime contract: controls as a page part, and an overflow policy on a wire for S116
data.description:
Why: a composer can't say which part the D-pad drives (ctx.controls.pad is a host convention), and when two strangers' Event maxes don't fit (S116) no glue can fix it: relay D stopped there (project/2026-11-26-placeholder-docs-findings.md). Ben ruled 2026-11-26 (note on Vv3lQY; project/2026-11-26-runtime-contract-plan.md, rulings 5 and 7).

What: (5) The page is a built-in part whose Event outputs are the controls. A glue wires them like any port, `.wire(page.<control>, <part>.<input>)`, with the usual frames, rename and S diagnostics. A part reads controls as Events, not by polling ctx.controls. Decide and document what the page part offers (at least the D-pad and buttons the DMG host has) and what a display run and a headless run feed it. (7) A wire may take `{ overflow: "keepLast" | "keepFirst" }`. With a policy, S116 is a warning naming the policy instead of an error; at run time the records past the consumer's max are dropped per the policy, counted in stats() and noted once per wire, as a stopped part's drops are (kit/run/README.md). The consumer's declared max never changes. The package reference (kit/package/reference.js) shows each Event port's max and delivery so S116 isn't a surprise.

Seams: kit/compose (compose.js, analyze.js, queues.js, codes.js), kit/run (scheduler, part.js, driver.js), kit/package/reference.js, scripts/seams-trial fixtures if they poll ctx.controls. Docs: kit/compose/README.md, kit/run/README.md, the seams doc a composer reads.

Out of scope: Program-derived Event maxes (backlog them in project/backlog.md with what would un-park them: a trial where a policy loses events a composer needed).

Open: whether ctx.controls goes away or stays for a part that runs alone. The agent's call; say which and why. Determinism: page Events must be recorded and replayed like inputs.

criteria.label: A test wires a page control to a part and shows the part receives it as an Event in a headless run, and that replay reproduces it.
A test shows S116 as an error without a policy and a warning naming the policy with one, and a run that overflows drops by keepLast and keepFirst as named, counted in stats() with one note per wire.
A generated reference.md lists each Event port with its max and delivery.
npm test and npm run typecheck pass; the docs say both.

data.title: Runtime contract: per-Program state, and defaults for optional Event input fields
data.description:
Why: a Program's own data (particles' `.field("<name>", …)`) has no place in a state the Dialect declares once. Relay authors packed fields into capped name/value lists or dropped them, so a field reset every step and no check noticed; it is the rerun's largest runtime gap. And every field an Event input declares must come from the producer, so authors kept inputs to the position alone and a composer can't pass more. Ben ruled 2026-11-26 (note on Vv3lQY; project/2026-11-26-runtime-contract-plan.md, rulings 2 and 4).

What: (2) A Dialect may mark one state member extensible; a Program's declarations add typed fields to it, checked against the built record, the way environment(program) already extends objects (kit/define/README.md). The runtime gets the extended shape, N003 (memory outside state) still holds over it, and there is no cap beyond the Program's own declarations. Replay and the content key cover the extension. (4) An Event input's field may declare a default, `<field>: <type> = <value>`; the wire fills it when the producer's record lacks the field, and a wire still never computes a value. A field without a default must still come from the producer (S diagnostics as today).

Seams: kit/define (dialect.js, record.js, shapes.js, ports.js, validate-dialect.js), kit/compose (wire analysis and filling), and in kit/run only where state is allocated and N003 is checked (part.js). Another agent owns kit/run/scheduler.js and the rest of part.js in parallel (rc-run): keep part.js edits small and say exactly what you changed there. Docs: kit/define/README.md, kit/START.md and kit/API.md in <placeholder> style (memory placeholders-not-examples).

Open: how a Dialect marks the extensible member and how a declaration maps to a field type. The agent's call, but run the shape past the dogfood rule (AGENTS.md "Dogfood our own designs") by keeping it close to environment(program); the runtime relay after this leaf is the dogfood.

Risks: the particles fixture in scripts/seams-trial must move off its name/value workaround (or the starting package must show the new way); say what changed.

criteria.label: A test declares an extensible state member, a Program adds two fields, and a runtime reads and writes them across steps; a write outside the extended shape is N003.
A test shows the content key and replay change when a declared field changes.
A test wires a producer whose record lacks a defaulted field and the consumer sees the default; a missing field with no default is still refused.
npm test and npm run typecheck pass; kit/define/README.md, kit/START.md and kit/API.md say both.

data.title: Review fixes for d8bba18, 7ae02ef, 73a6c06, 829ddef: concat mixed run, stale L008 tip, condition tips, S301 gaps, G008
data.description:
reviewer-kit-4 (2026-11-26) reviewed d8bba18, 7ae02ef, 73a6c06, 829ddef. Probes in /Users/ben/git/workbench/local/rev-kit-4/ (run `node local/rev-kit-4/<name>` from the repo root); each confirmed probe is the fix's red test, ported into the module's tests.

1. HIGH (73a6c06), c3b-mixed-run.probe.mjs: a mixed-type run beside a spread lowers with no diagnostic. `(a) => [1, 'x', ...a]` gives ok: true, diagnostics [], returns "unknown", verify V003/V002, run null. Plain `[1, 'x']` is L003. Cause: concat() in kit/lower/expr.js (~665-680) builds the run's array part with t "unknown" and reports nothing; the later `if (p.t === "unknown") return bad(node)` returns silently. Report L003 in the run thunk as array() does. Also have kit/ir/verify.js refuse a concat part whose item type is "unknown".
2. MEDIUM (7ae02ef), c2c-l008-tip.probe.mjs: L008's tip (kit/lower/expr.js:280 and :318) says `if (!e) return;`, which bool-only conditions now refuse (L003). Tip must say `if (e == null) return;`. Same stale advice in kit/lower/README.md (List indexing, ~line 30: `if (!m) return;`; nominal scalars ~38: narrows "by truthiness") and the scalarTest doc comment in kit/lower/scalar.js (~62-68). Grep the kit and docs for other `if (!` tips.
3. LOW (7ae02ef), c2-bool.probe.mjs: conditionTip gives `x !== 0` for a list, struct or null-typed value (itself L003) and `x !== ""` for an enum (always true). Give a correct tip per type (list: `x.length !== 0`; struct: a field; enum: `x === "<member>"`), and parenthesize the source text when it is not a simple name or member chain (`(b ? n : n) !== 0`).
4. LOW (d8bba18), c1-handle.probe.mjs: the S301 glue scan misses a handle in `switch (h)`, `h in obj`, sequence expressions `(0, h) ? …`, and `(flag && h) === 1` (caught before the commit; the right-operand rule only matches a direct chain). Flag these.
5. LOW (829ddef), c4-bornnear.probe.mjs (role particles): G008 passes a misplaced burst plus a following marker, because bornNear takes min(near diff, total diff). Count only particles born within the radius. Also make bornNear throw (or report) when its baseline is undefined instead of counting pre-existing particles.

data.title: Review fixes for 883c7b0: display runUntil restart backlog, chunk-invariant frames, restart timing, driver window
data.description:
reviewer-run-3 (2026-11-26) reviewed 883c7b0 (leaf 4WMA0R). Probes in /Users/ben/git/workbench/local/rev-run-3/ (run `node <path>` from the repo root; they import the main checkout's kit, so port each into kit/run/test and see it red there). Its fuzzers (stop-restart-fuzz, consumer-stop-fuzz, driver-rununtil-fuzz, s116-demand-frame-fuzz) held at HEAD and must still hold after the fix.

Integrator rulings (2026-11-26, Ben away; two-way doors, reported to Ben):
- R1, display runUntil is chunk-invariant: on a display run, runUntil logs frames only on the nominal grid from the last frame (lastFrame + k/60 <= target) and never adds a frame at the target. So runUntil(1) in one go and runUntil(0.31) then runUntil(1) give the same frames, instants and hashes. Update kit/run/README.md (Run control; "frame parts step through a skip ahead as they would headless" then becomes true).
- R2, a restart does not depend on unrelated parts: a build or input that restarts a part takes effect at its own stamp; the restarted part's first instant is the first on its clock at or after that stamp, whatever other parts are in the composition (finding 4: with a 1 s ticker, a 1/8 s part restarted at 1.01 must step at 9/8, not wait for 2). Record it in project/2026-11-25-clocks-draft.md's rulings block.
- R3, N001 for stopped drops is noted once per wire per stop (cleared on restart), not once per run.

Findings:
1. HIGH, display-restart-backlog.probe.mjs: a frame part restarted during a display runUntil gets a backlog and N002 (41 records, max 4) though S116 accepted the wiring; the consumer never steps again, and the outcome depends on chunking. logFrames runs once at runUntil's start and only if a frame part is running; after a mid-chunk restart no frames are logged. Also the first frame of the next chunk can land more than a cap after the last (`cmp(cap, now) > 0` clamp). Same path for a frame part whose init failed and is fixed mid-chunk.
2. MEDIUM, display-chunk.probe.mjs: frames logged by runUntil depend on chunking (60 vs 61 frames). Fix per R1.
3. MEDIUM, display-rununtil-noframe.probe.mjs: after runUntil on a display run with no running frame part, the driver's next frame is capped from a stale lastFrame and N001 reports a bogus 293x. The driver's window must agree with run.T.
4. MEDIUM, restart-unrelated-ticker.probe.mjs: fix per R2.
5. LOW, edges.probe.mjs (a): a frame part fixed at T = 0 on a display run skips the frame at 0 (nextFrame's framesBefore(floor) misses the implied frame at 0).
6. LOW, edges.probe.mjs (b): step() with no part due applies every input however far ahead (upcoming(null)) and returns null; a later input then throws a wrong message ("the run is at its start"). step() should apply at most up to the next due instant (or document and fix the message); README's step row must say what it does.
7. LOW: docs and a test. README Real-time "Frames are kept to the millisecond", the driver.js header and log.js afterMs comment are untrue for runUntil frames (fix per R1 or reword). window.test.js:218 asserts `s <= 1/60 + 1e-12 || s <= 0.1`, equivalent to `s <= 0.1`: make it test what it means. The clocks draft body still uses R001/R004 where kit/run uses N-codes: add a correction note.

data.title: Review fixes for 8b5c171: fill always wins, rename-masking warning, N003 message, nested extensible, D028 tip, shared fill arrays
data.description:
reviewer-define-5 (2026-11-26) reviewed 8b5c171 (leaf 62J2dk). Probes in /Users/ben/git/workbench/local/rev-define-5/ (run `node local/rev-define-5/<name>.probe.mjs` from the repo root; they import the main checkout's kit, so port each into the module's tests and see it red there).

Integrator rulings (2026-11-26, Ben away; reported to him):
- F1: a wire's planned fill always wins. Compose decided statically that the producer's seam lacks the field, so a stray undeclared field a runtime pushes under that name is replaced by the default, never passed through.
- F2: a wire that both drops a producer field and fills a consumer field whose seam types are compatible gets a warning (a new S2xx code, next free in kit/compose/codes.js) naming the likely rename as the fix: `rename: { <dropped>: "<filled>" }`. A warning, not an error: the default may be intended.

Findings:
1. MEDIUM, fill.probe.mjs case A: kit/run/carry.js fills only when !Object.hasOwn(o, k), so a runtime that pushes an undeclared `speed: "not-a-number"` reaches a consumer whose `speed: f64 = 40` the plan says it fills. Fix per F1.
2. MEDIUM, fill.probe.mjs case B: producer { n, velocity: f64 }, consumer { n, vel: f64 = 0 }, no rename: check() is clean (was S202 before). Fix per F2; case F (an explicit rename wins, fills nothing) must still hold.
3. LOW, state-extend.probe.mjs "outside + misfit mix": stateProblem in kit/run/part.js reports only the outside mismatches when a state also misfits. Report both (N003, listing the misfits too).
4. LOW, state-extend.probe.mjs "decl extensible struct again": a Program-declared field typed struct({…}, { extensible: true }) is accepted; make it D023 (one extensible struct per state, and a Program's fields are not extensible).
5. LOW, tip.probe.mjs: D028's tip for a record-typed field default suggests `{ x: 0 }`, which the seam grammar can't parse (sampleDefault in kit/define/ports.js). Say a record-typed field takes no default.
6. LOW, fill.probe.mjs case D: deepFreeze(carry(rec, w)) freezes the shared fill arrays (the Dialect's parsed seam defaults) in place. Have carry copy each filled value (a list default is a fresh array per record).
7. LOW: kit/run/scheduler.js Wire typedef (line ~34) lacks `fill`. Routed to runtime-fix-3, which owns scheduler.js; not this leaf's.
SUSPECTED (not for this leaf): the per-record WeakMap in kit/define/dialect.js goes stale if a built record is mutated in place; no in-tree code does. Noted in the backlog only if it bites.

data.title: Rulings needed: draw-list draft changes from the paper trial
data.description:
The draw-list paper trial (e3qYus, project/2026-11-26-draw-list-trial-findings.md, "Recommendations") found three premises of the ruled draft to change before Draw is built, plus a ruling on builders. Each changes what a package author writes, so each is Ben's call. The recommendations are the trial's; the integrator agrees with them.

1. A Draw max from the built record, as extent(record) does, with a Dialect-level ceiling. (Recommended.)
2. The Game Boy check at composition: give the seam an op mix (`Draw<image 38, tiles 1, text 40>@<frame>`), or check only op kinds at composition and counts at draw time. (Integrator leans to kinds-only at composition: smaller surface, and the count check at draw time is exact.)

4. What a builder may read: the record and value inputs (Draw inputs through the inputs global), or rule that a root mirrors them into state. (Recommended: builders read the record and inputs.)
5. Per-item over non-entity state: give `each` an index, or document that an entity-style Dialect keeps an entity list in state (the findings lean to documenting it, plus a tiles op the grid can feed).
6. Spell out the small items listed in the findings (from-layer counting, negative size/r, alpha on 4 shades, text formatting, Draw input waking a demand part, which Draw output the page shows) — no ruling needed, a doc pass during the build.

Waiting on this: the Draw build leaf under FqsPVJ.

data.title: kit/run and kit/compose: review fixes for 5e0813e ($T stamping, page bound, part named page, page input edges, overflow validation)
data.description:
Review of 5e0813e by reviewer-rc-8 (2026-11-26). Probes: local/rev-5e0813e/*.probe.js, run with plain node. All confirmed by the integrator rerunning them.

HIGH 1, $T stamping (kit/run/wires.js:514-516 stamped(); carry() returns the same object when a wire has no rename/drop/convert/fill). stamped() stamps only unfrozen records and freezes the caller's object in place. Results: dev runs lose $T when a producer keeps its pushed record in state (stamp-dev); frozen records get no $T; a reused object gets a stale $T; the host's pad object is frozen, so its next write throws (stamp-frozen); a JSON round-tripped log fails replay with N005 (stamp-replay). Fix: always copy, then stamp, then freeze. Clone a page input's value when it is logged.

HIGH 2, the page bound (kit/compose/page.js:49-55 sizes the page as one record per control per frame; kit/run/scheduler.js:365 delivers one per run.input call). Two pad changes in one frame stop a consumer with events.in.pad: 1 (page-frame.probe.js 1), and 69 headless inputs stop a max-64 tick consumer (page-burst). Integrator's call (reversible, reported to Ben): coalesce page inputs to the last value per control per instant, so the composition-time bound holds.

MEDIUM, a user part named "page" (scheduler.js:156, :165 test e.part === PAGE only): its controls get routed to page wires and refused (page-edges C, C2). Fix: route by whether a page part exists; S101 already covers the clash once a page wire exists.

LOW: (1) a page input is checked when logged but delivered by reference, so a later host mutation changes it (page-edges A); (2) a page input to a composition with no page part is dropped silently, where any other unknown part throws (page-edges D); (3) createRun does not validate `overflow` in a composed record: any truthy value skips S116 (scheduler.js:324, wires.js:554) and acts as keepFirst (delivery.js:215).

Also from the reviewer: replay tests should round-trip the record through JSON.

data.title: kit/build why text: review fixes (superseded builds, input attribution, off-grid boundary wording, since count, unknown part)
data.description:
Review of the why-text commit (9GMTBs) by reviewer-why-10. Probes are in local/rev-why-10/ (run with `node <file>` from the repo root). The integrator confirmed why3.
1. MEDIUM: two rebuilds of one part between two steps of its consumer. The consumers line claims the consumer read X@2 from its first step at or after the boundary, but it read X@3, and no step ever read X@2. With two builds at the same stamp it gets worse: level@3 claims steps read level@2, level@2's inputs line lists both rebuild inputs, and level@3's lists none (inputsText is exclusive of the previous boundary and inclusive of this one). Probes: why.probe.js §2 and why3.probe.js. Fix: word a superseded build as superseded (the next build of the same part lands before any consumer step), and attribute inputs to builds by log position, not by time.
2. LOW: "before instant T=<stamp>" names an instant that never runs when the stamp is off the instant grid (why2.probe.js). Suggested wording: "after instant T=1/5, at T=41/200 (before the next instant)".
3. LOW: "N rebuilds in the run log" counts only the builds after since (why.probe.js §3). Say "N rebuilds since T=…".
4. LOW: run.why("nosuch") claims that part exists; run.why should refuse an unknown part.
5. LOW, no fix: float time comparisons go wrong only near T = 2^53.

data.title: kit/draw: lower Draw builders through kit/lower and drop the globalThis binding
data.description: From the Draw build (GCy994, commit "Adds Draw…"). The draft's ruling 1 says a picture is built by Bench code, not trusted JS. As built, kit/draw/builders.js only scans builders (J002 refuses map and its kin, and the scan reads the op kinds) and then runs them as plain JS, setting the inputs and params globals on globalThis while they run (withGlobals). data.title: kit/run param wires: review fixes (same-stamp idempotency, display-mode stamps, type in the key, rebuilt defaults, handle nit)
data.description:
Review of 5db1d27 by reviewer-pw-12. Probes are in local/rev-pw-12/ (run with `node <file>`). The integrator confirmed 1 and 2.
1. HIGH, a host param input at a wire input's stamp breaks replay (N005), and the replay applies the wire twice (host-same-stamp.probe.js). The default stamp of run.input is the next instant, which is the wire's stamp, so this is the ordinary host call. Cause: kit/run/param-wires.js:41-46. The "already logged" test looks only at the param's last entry at or before the stamp. Fix direction: identify a wire input by its wire and the instant that made it (log the source instant on the entry), and treat any such entry as already logged.
2. HIGH, in a display run the wire's stamp depends on which frames are logged yet (display.probe.js): the stamps differ between a chunked run, a whole run and a replay, with N005 at 7/60 and the wire applied twice per change. This also breaks R2. Cause: scheduler.js:136, `nextInstant() ?? afterMs(lastT)` is computed before the next frame is logged. Invariant: a wire input's stamp must be a function of the instant that made it alone, landing before any later instant.
3. LOW, keyed() drops `value`, and a declaration's type comes only from its value, so a change of a param's type alone keeps the key and the compiled code (key.probe.js). Fix: keep typeof value (or the declared type) in the keyed declaration. SUSPECTED: a runtime's init(record) or clock(record) reading record.params.<n>.value. Decide whether kit/define forbids that, and document it.
4. Pre-existing: a rebuild input whose record changes a param's declared default, or adds a param, never reaches $ (p.params is set only at part.js:189 and scheduler.js:193).
5. Nit: b.param.call, .bind or .length for an undeclared name returns the function's own property, not a known:false handle, so the error is S102, not S111.
Also: the commit message's "for any host chunk" holds in nominal mode only. Add display-mode tests.

data.title: kit/run/draw.js and builders: Draw review fixes (per-part list cache, layer max validation, derived concat max, draw-time profile check)
data.description:

Two parts whose runtimes return the same object (an init that returns a module constant, a step that returns s) show each other's lists (compose.probe.js B). data.text: fix-pw-14: all five findings fixed in worktree agent-ab51d9fef082a742c (branch worktree-agent-ab51d9fef082a742c), uncommitted. Stamp rule chosen: a param wire's input is stamped with the instant that made it and applied right after that instant (applyInputs stops before instant T at the first wire input stamped T). Not afterMs: two instants can share a millisecond (sub-ms ticks; a 1/60 s tick beside a ms display frame), so +1 ms can land after the next instant. Build boundary for it is { after: T, before: T }; why.js reads that as "right after instant T" and compares boundaries as pairs. Finding 3: valueType kept in keyed(); kit/define documents runtimes read values via ctx.params only (no runtime reads record.params.<n>.value). data.title: Draw review fixes: rewind of a stopped producer and of params, expected-list rule vs verify, builder globals
data.description:
Review of 81657d6 and a2dfa1d by reviewer-draw-16. Probes are in local/rev-draw-16/ (run with `node <file>`; lower-nonunion needs `node --import ./kit/test/verify-lowering.js`).
F1 HIGH: a stopped producer's lists vanish on rewind. redraw (end of part.js) sets draws to NONE when p.stopped, while a straight run keeps reading the last lists (stopped-rewind.probe.js: hashes differ at 5/8 and 7/8). Fix: rebuild whenever the state is not null.
F2 HIGH: redraw builds with the current p.params, not the params the lists were built with. A param input or a same-key rebuild changes $ without redrawing, so a checkpoint in that gap redraws "K 7" where the straight run shows "K 1" (param-rewind.probe.js). Fix: carry drawParams with drawValues, or the frozen draws themselves.
F3 MEDIUM: kit/lower's fitsWanted (end of expr.js) accepts any expected item type each item fits; kit/ir/verify's declaredItem (verify.js:528) accepts only a union. So lowering accepts and verify reports V002, in every Dialect (lower-nonunion.probe.js, five cases; draw-points.probe.js: `points: [p, [k, 1]]`, uneven tiles grid rows). With verify off this silently accepts lists the README documents as refused. Make the two agree (limit fitsWanted to a union, as the commit message says, or widen declaredItem) and update kit/lower/README.md.
F5 LOW: a builder may read any Dialect global at lowering (draw-lower.js copies base.globals), but gets only $ and the inputs at run time, so it fails as J022 (global-read.probe.js). Ruling 4: limit the builder environment's globals at lowering.

data.title: Game Boy profile: painter's order, sprite x priority, 8x16 mode, VRAM tile count

SUSPECTED: 8x16 sprite mode isn't modeled (16-tall images counted as two), and a sheet's tile count is never checked against VRAM (256 background tiles).

Proposal awaiting his confirmation: a built-in `layer` part (like `page`) whose Draw inputs take their ceilings from the wired producers, whose output max is their sum, and whose frame extent comes from the bottom layer. `.show(a.out.view, b.out.view)` would be sugar that inserts one. 2026-11-27, Ben asked whether authors only need to fake Events, or need scripted input separately. Answer given: they are one mechanism (a script is a list of timed fake records on a named input; kit/run can already do it). The gaps are access (a package may not import kit/run) and a place to declare tests with expectations. # Findings: the layer draft, dogfooded by three blind composers

*2026-11-27, leaf `teBNYM` (container `XlXLSp`). The local dogfood ruling (AGENTS.md): fresh agents use a design before it is frozen, and their difficulty is feedback on the design. The design is the layer draft in [kit/compose/README.md](../kit/compose/README.md), "Layers (draft)" (leaf `LiOmY9`), under Ben's ruling of the same day ([the plan](2026-11-27-layer-and-package-tests-plan.md), "Rulings" 1).*

## Summary

The draft held. Three blind Sonnet 5.5 composers, each given the M4 trial's two packages and the kit docs with the draft, wrote the M4 timed-gems glue against it. All three were clean at their first check, rated the task 1 of 5, used the `.show(<output>, <output>)` shorthand, and wrote no package of their own. **The massage was 0 lines.** That is down from a 30-line glue plus a 70-line `overlay` package on 2026-11-26. Their glues are 28 to 33 lines (`wc -l`), and none copies a Draw ceiling or a canvas size.

What they could not get from the draft was **placement**. Each worked out the score panel's offset by hand from the two extents ((192 − 160) / 2 = 16), and two of them said this contradicts the draft's "no extent is typed twice". Each also guessed which way a `.frame` edge maps. The draft now says the edge's direction, and says that the layer derives ceilings and the box but not where a picture sits. An anchored edge is parked in the backlog as a `.frame` question.

The dogfood also found that **the draft's own worked example was wrong**. It gave the M4 layer as `Draw<310>` (302 + 8). Those are the Dialects' declared ceilings; the built maxes for that level and round are 67 and 5, so the layer is `Draw<72>`. The checker computed 72, and the draft is corrected in place.

None of the three judgment calls the drafter flagged was tested. No leg named a layer, made one with a single input or a doubled input, or showed one output alone, so there is no evidence for or against the fixed name `layers` or for the two S102 refusals. Nothing here bears on Ben's ruling.

## The runs

The setup has three parts:

- **Packages.** Each leg got the 2026-11-26 trial's hand-ins as that composer got them: `runs/2026-11-26/game-run1/gemgrid` and `runs/2026-11-26/score/scoretimer`. `diff -r` against the copies in `runs/2026-11-26/compose/` is empty. No leg got the `overlay` package.
- **Docs.** Each leg got the kit docs the trial copies. `scripts/m4-trial/layer-docs.js` then edited the copies:
  - It left the draft section in `compose/README.md`, minus its own rewrite of the M4 glue (see Deviations).
  - It added the drafter's two integration lines to `START.md` and `API.md`, marked draft.
  - It dropped "a composed page that layers parts" from API.md's Not built.
- **Task.** The task was `scripts/m4-trial/docs/task-layer.md`: the compose task, saying that layering is built in per the draft, that a package of the composer's own is not allowed, and that long docs are read with the Read tool by offset.

The checker is a stand-in, because the layer is not built (below).

```sh
R=scripts/m4-trial/runs/2026-11-26
scripts/m4-trial/run.sh layer /private/tmp/teBNYM-1 sonnet $R/game-run1 $R/score   # likewise teBNYM-2 and teBNYM-3, run in parallel
node scripts/seams-trial/summary.js scripts/m4-trial/runs/2026-11-27-layer/leg1 scripts/m4-trial/runs/2026-11-27-layer/leg2 scripts/m4-trial/runs/2026-11-27-layer/leg3 --skip-last
```

| Leg | Checks | Codes; first clean | Turns | Time | Cost | Difficulty | Massage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | none; run 1 | 11 | 48 s | $0.30 | 1 | 0 lines |
| 2 | 3 | none (an S206 warning on an experiment); run 1 | 12 | 49 s | $0.26 | 1 | 0 lines |
| 3 | 3 | none (an S206 warning on an experiment); run 1 | 14 | 69 s | $0.33 | 1 | 0 lines |

Turns, time and cost come from `summary.js` as above, which reads each transcript's result line. Difficulty is each leg's own REPORT.md. The massage comes from reading each hand-in by hand against the draft.

For comparison, the 2026-11-26 composer (Sonnet 5.5, `run.sh compose`) took 16 turns, 77 s and $0.54. The task was the same, but that composer had to write the layering package.

**Blindness held.** No transcript reads a file outside its leg folder, and none opens a saved tool result. Each read the long docs with the Read tool, as the task asked. Every leg read `compose/README.md`; leg 1 also read `draw/README.md` and `page/README.md`, and leg 3 `draw/README.md`. Checked with `grep -o '"file_path":"[^"]*"'` and `grep -c tool-results` over each `transcript.jsonl`. The legs did `cat` their own package files and `START.md`, which are short.

### The hand-ins, read by hand

All three glues have the same shape:

```js
.part(<game>).part(<round>)
.frame(<round>.frame.panel, <game>.frame.px, { scale: 1, offset: [16, <0 or 4>] })
.wire(page.out.pad, <game>.in.pad)
.wire(<game>.out.picked, <round>.in.scored, { set: { points: 1 } })
.show(<game>.out.view, <round>.out.view)
```

Against the draft, each glue:

- **Painter's order:** the game first, at the bottom. Each said so in a comment or its report.
- **Root package:** none.
- **Draw ceiling:** none in the text. The checker's T031 scan for a producer's declared or built max, a layer's sum, or the bottom extent found nothing.
- **Frames:** relates the top producer's frame to the bottom one's directly, with no third canvas.
- **Wires and imports:** otherwise valid. On the real kit the composition (minus the layer, with the bottom producer shown) checks and builds, and plays the pad script to a score.

Each made the level's top two rows wall, so the 24-pixel panel hides no play. Leg 3 made the level 9 rows tall. The layer the draft would make, as the checker prints it:

- **Legs 1 and 2:** `Draw<72>@<game>.px`, page box 192 by 128.
- **Leg 3:** `Draw<82>@level.px`, page box 192 by 144.

The 2026-11-26 composer's map also had two wall rows under the panel, at the same offset `[16, 4]` that leg 2 chose. That composer's glue was not in any leg's folder, and the transcripts show no leg reading outside its folder, so this is two runs reaching the same layout from the same packages, not a leak.

### What misled them, and what they guessed

| Finding | Legs | What the draft said | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Which way `.frame(a, b, { scale, offset })` maps | 1, 2, 3 | nothing; the main API table doesn't say either. All guessed `b = a × scale + offset`, which is right | the draft says it ("Placing a picture") |
| Placing a smaller picture needs an offset computed from both extents, against "no extent is typed twice" | 1, 2, 3 (2 and 3 named the contradiction) | that no extent is typed twice | the draft says the layer derives the ceilings and the canvas box, not the placement; an anchored edge is parked in `project/backlog.md` |
| A conversion never scales `text`, so a HUD wants scale 1, and `"fit"` would scale it | 1, 3 (leg 3: "text is the main thing a score overlay draws") | nothing | said in "Placing a picture" |
| Whether `.show(<output>, <output>)` adds the outputs' parts | 1, 2, 3 (each added both with `.part` to be safe) | the layer joins at first mention; "a handle of a part not added" is S102, in the codes paragraph only | a row in the API table: producers are added with `.part`, and naming an output adds nothing |
| Whether an upper picture's ops outside the bottom box are clipped | 3 | nothing | the canvas is sized to the box, so ops outside it fall off, as for any shown list |
| What the page shows of each part's UI (tiles) when a layer is shown | 3 | nothing | each part's tiles, inputs and params as today; the host's fallback stage never applies to a layer. **Build seam:** kit/page/host's `textStage` looks a package up by the shown name |
| The main tables (`.show` takes "one"; S102 for `.show` of a non-part) disagree with the draft | 2 | nothing | the draft's head says it wins over those rows until the build changes them |
| `START.md`'s draft line reads as present tense ("the glue layers them") | 2 | the copy carried "(draft)" only at the end | none: at layer-build the line goes in unmarked, so the tense will be right |

Two findings are not about the layer:

- **S206 suggests a harmful rename.** Legs 2 and 3 tried the pickup wire without `set` and got S206: "cannot feed … rename `collected` to `points`". `collected` is a running total, so that rename would score 1, 2, 3 and so on. The warning also opens with "cannot feed" though the wire works. Not changed here (kit/compose, out of scope). The 2026-11-26 composer chose `set` for the same reason.
- **Checker defect, fixed.** The stand-in's S206 was placed at `layer-draft.js:117`, the stand-in's own line, joined onto the leg's folder. kit/compose places a diagnostic at the innermost stack frame outside its own modules, and for a forwarded call that is the stand-in. The checker now places a real diagnostic at the glue call whose handles name its sides. Regression test: `scripts/m4-trial/test/layer.test.js`, "a real kit diagnostic about a forwarded call…". Both legs reported the path without opening it.

Leg 3 also said the task's "fails on any diagnostic" was wrong, since an S206 warning passed. `task-layer.md` now says "any error".

## The checker: what a program could check

`node scripts/m4-trial/check.js <leg> --role layer --given <game package> --given <score package>`, documented in [scripts/m4-trial/README.md](../scripts/m4-trial/README.md).

How it loads a glue:

- It loads the glue as the page host does, except that `kit/compose` resolves to `checker/layer-draft.js`. That module re-exports kit/compose and adds the draft's `layer`. Its `compose` forwards every call to a real composition, except the draft's own calls, which it records.
- It judges the records with the draft's codes, printed `(draft)`: S101, S102, S111, S201, S204, S251 and S404.
- S251's frame graph is built from each part's own lowered edges and the glue's `.frame` calls, as kit/compose builds its own.
- It prints each layer as the draft would make it: its summed max from the built Programs (kit/define's lowered `seams.draws`), its frame, its page box, and each input's conversion.
- It then builds the real composition with the shown layer's bottom producer shown, and plays the compose leg's pad script on it.

The leg's own codes:

- T030: a package beside the given two.
- T031: a warning for review, a copied ceiling or extent.
- T032: the shown thing is not a layer of both pictures.
- T033: the score is under the game.

What it cannot check:

- It cannot draw the layer or read its picture, so T025 (an image drawn) and T011 (a picture drawn) check the bottom picture only.
- It does not follow S401 through a layer, or a wire from a layer into a part that is then played.
- A frame-path disagreement (S253) between a layer's inputs is left to the real `.frame` checks.

So every hand-in was also read by hand, as above. The draft's own rewrite of the M4 glue checks clean under it, which is where `Draw<72>` came from.

## Draft changes

All of these are in `kit/compose/README.md`, "Layers (draft)", still marked draft:

1. **The head** says the dogfood revised the section. It also says the section wins over the `.show` row and the S102 row of the tables above, until the build changes them.
2. **The opening paragraph** says "no ceiling and no canvas size is typed", in place of "no extent is typed twice", and points to placement.
3. **A new API row, "the producers":** each output's part is added with `.part`, and naming an output adds nothing (S102).
4. **"What the page draws, and its box"** now covers:
   - ops outside the box fall off the canvas;
   - each part's tiles, inputs and params show as today;
   - the build seam in kit/page/host's `textStage`.
5. **A new decision, "Placing a picture":**
   - the edge's direction;
   - scale 1 for a picture of text, with the reason;
   - `"fit"` is for a background;
   - the offset is the composer's, and the anchored edge is parked.
6. **The M4 rewrite's summed max** is corrected in place: `Draw<72>`, 67 + 5, not `Draw<310>`.

Not changed, for want of evidence:

- the shorthand's fixed name `layers`;
- the S102 refusals of a one-input layer, a doubled input and `.show(<one output>)`;
- named ports against argument order. Every leg found the argument order plain.

## Questions for Ben

None that would change the ruling. Two smaller calls are the drafter's or the builder's, and are written down here:

- **The anchored edge.** Should the layer stage take on an anchored `.frame` edge? All three legs asked for one. This report parks it as a `.frame` question for every wire, not the layer's.
- **S206's suggested rename** can be harmful when the dropped field is a running total, as here. That is a kit/compose follow-up, not filed here.

## Deviations

- **The legs' compose README had no worked example.** The draft's subsection "The M4 trial's glue, rewritten against this draft" was dropped from their copy. It is this task's answer, with the real part names, map and offsets, and a leg given it would be tested on copying. ("Placeholders, not examples": examples get copied.) The integration lines and the rest of the draft were given whole.
- **The given packages came from the author legs' folders.** They are `runs/2026-11-26/game-run1` and `runs/2026-11-26/score`, not `runs/2026-11-26/compose/`. `run.sh` takes a leg folder with exactly one package, and the compose record holds three. The two copies are byte-identical (`diff -r`, and T027).

data.title: Anchor: draft an anchored .frame edge
data.description:
Why: all five blind composers on 2026-11-27 (three layer dogfood legs, the Sonnet and Haiku closing legs) placed the HUD panel by computing a `.frame` offset by hand ((192 − 160) / 2 = 16), and every one asked for an anchored edge; the Haiku leg named `anchor: "bottom-center"`. A hand offset goes stale when a picture's size changes, and `"fit"` cannot help because a draw list's text never scales. Ben un-parked it on 2026-11-27 ("I guess we should design the anchor API"). Evidence: project/2026-11-27-layer-dogfood-findings.md, project/2026-11-27-layer-rerun-findings.md, and the backlog entry "an anchored frame edge" in project/backlog.md.

What: a draft, as documentation an agent can build against, of a `.frame` edge form that computes its offset from the two frames' extents: a new section at the end of kit/compose/README.md marked draft, with placeholder snippets (<part>, <frame>), never made-up names. Settle: the vocabulary (which anchors: edges, corners, center; per axis or named points), a margin or inset, how it combines with `scale` (scale 1 only, or any scale), what an anchored edge needs (both frames must have an extent: the code when one lacks it), when the offset is computed (from the built records' extents at build time, so a rebuild that changes an extent changes it; say how kit/run sees that), how the plan prints it, and how it interacts with `"fit"` and existing edges (S253 disagreements, chains). Keep the surface small (Ben: "A smaller and simpler API surface is always better if possible"): prefer one option over several.

Seams: kit/compose (frame edges, the frame graph, plan printing, layer frames), kit/define frames' `extent(record)`, kit/run (whether a rebuilt extent moves an edge), kit/seam.

Out of scope: building it; the layer part itself (built).

Open: anything that changes the layer ruling goes to Ben; the rest is the drafter's call, with reasons.

data.title: Decide: page buttons share one seam, so a part run alone gets no button wired (H009)
data.description: Decision for Ben, from tests-build-40 (ceE4ib, 0639eb3). With ctx.controls retired, examplePreset wires each page control to the one Event input whose seam is exactly the control's. The four buttons (a, b, start, select) share one seam, Event<{ held: bool }>, so a part run alone with any button input fits four controls and gets none wired (H009, a warning): solo button input no longer works, where controls.a did. Ben's ruling (2026-11-27) was to refuse with a clear code when two inputs take one control, with no naming convention; this is the other direction (one input, several controls), which seams alone can never settle for buttons. Options: (a) break a tie by name: in.<control> takes page.out.<control> when seams alone are ambiguous (a convention, but only a tiebreak); (b) give each button its own seam (e.g. a tag field), so seams decide; (c) keep refusing, and a part that wants a button needs a glue. Recommendation: (a). Also tell Ben: H009 is a warning (the example still loads, unwired), not an error; and a held pad no longer survives a rebuild (it lives in part state; the page sends only changes), documented in kit/run/README.md.

data.text: Ben, 2026-11-27: 'In general, I don't want to drag in dependencies, so some of these will require first-principles thinking.' Relayed to all four feasibility agents: no new dependencies; browser standards (WebGPU, Web Audio, Web MIDI, WebAssembly, FontFace, Canvas) are not dependencies; QuickJS would be one.

feas-lang-50 findings (read-only): Bench cannot lex/parse user text today: str has no length/index/charCodeAt (L002/L009), lists cannot be stored into (L012) or grown in a loop (L003), helpers cannot recurse (L007). A DFA over a list of char codes with scalar state lowers OK. Probe: local/feas-lang-50/kuwxBq-probe.js. Recommendation: the playground's lexer/parser is host code (a kit module or the package runtime) interpreting the grammar the Program declares; QuickJS-as-front-end is unwise (dynamic untyped bytecode, no spans/maxes, ~0.8 MB dependency) - grow the subset (monomorphized Library generics, fixed-size mutable local arrays, Library as lib/*.js files) instead. Full report handed back to coordinator.

feas-type-49 findings (Grotesk, Book), summary; full report handed back to the coordinator.
- Draw has no curves, one contour per op, one font ("mono", 8 units, never scales): kit/draw/ops.js:12-24. Both sketches need a path op (cubic/quadratic, multiple contours, fill rule) and sized text or glyph-outline drawing.
- Bench cannot build variable-length lists (no push, empty [] L012, no store into list[i], lists of different len don't join; kit/lower/README.md:30-34), so overlap removal, line breaking and pagination are runtime (trusted JS) work, not Kernels. Fixed-topology glyph construction IS expressible in Bench (concat sums maxes).
- Text/json/csv data files are loaded and checked but never reach a runtime or Program (kit/run/part.js:128 ctx; only images reach the page via kit/page/sources.js:27). S gap, and it blocks Book's Markdown input.
- A workbench of demand parts only makes no instant (kit/run/README.md:118, not built): both sketches are timeless.
- No exporter / file-to-viewer path; foreign modules are declared but nothing calls them. Artifact text save() verified in M0; binary download untested.
- No pointer, text-entry, double-click or source write-back; params edit the run, not the source.
- Font metrics must be data (a run is a pure function of record+params+log), so host measureText is unwise; Grotesk's font seam supplies metrics and outlines.

feas-audio-48 findings (summary; full report to coordinator):
- kit/run headless at tick 1/48000 (trivial state, dev=false): 5 s audio in 806 ms but heap +85 MB (240001 hashes kept, unbounded); per-block 128/48000 with a 16-voice x 6-op state: 5 s in 659 ms (dev=false), 1283 ms (dev=true). Bench: local/feas-audio-48/K4CaKm-*.bench.js. So per-block on kit/run's contract is affordable; per-sample instants are not (memory).
- The page's fold (kit/run README, The page part) assumes every page record is the whole held state; note on/off records are deltas, so a chord past PAGE_CHANGES_PER_FRAME (2) loses notes. Note input needs a delta-kind control with reliable delivery.
- Real time is driven by display frames (rAF); audio needs the audio clock as master and a worklet runner. kit/run uses structuredClone, which AudioWorkletGlobalScope likely lacks (INFERRED).
- defineUI stage emits ["pick","select","param"] are validated but no host listens (grep of kit/).
- Web MIDI: none in Safari (WebKit bug 107250); midi permissions policy default self, so a cross-origin artifact iframe needs allow="midi"; whether claude.ai grants it is unverified (needs a probe).

feas-optics-47: report handed back to the coordinator. Key numbers (probes in local/feas-optics-47/): kit/build stateHash on a 512x512x3 accumulation buffer held in run state = 122 ms per commit (256^2: 17 ms); checkState 17 ms; copy 12 ms; freeze 9 ms; a Float32Array is refused by checkState ("expected a list"). So an image buffer cannot live in a part's state: the image must be derived (like Draw lists), with state holding only the sample count. Biggest gaps: (1) a GPU image pipeline (WGSL emitter from LIR + float targets, multi-pass, storage buffers, an Image stage/seam); (2) scene-as-data across seams (no cross-package Kernels or shared libraries); (3) stage input + source write-back (pointer/pick/drag, builder-literal rewrite; params write-back is NOT built in the kit).

The draft says which are its stage and which are later stages. Test workbenches beyond DMG: the FM synth (notes, knobs, MIDI as a host), Grotesk (handles bound to builder args, text entry), the lens bench (pointer drag, catalog picker, tabs). Source write-back is not built at all (M4 promised it).

data.title: CPU tier: design one language, two tiers (a heap IR beside Bench)
data.description:
Why: Ben's ruling 2 in project/2026-11-27-sketch-feasibility-findings.md ("Rulings"). Heavy algorithms (parsers, line breaking, pagination, overlap removal, font writing, optimizers, voice allocation) cannot be Kernels: Bench's IR has no heap (no growable lists, strings, while or recursion) because GPU targets cannot host one. Today they would be unchecked package runtime JS.
What: a design draft (a dated project/ doc, placeholder snippets) of "one language, two tiers": the same JS subset and parser (kit/parse); a CPU-tier IR with a heap (growable lists with or without a declared capacity, strings with indexing and length, while, recursion, maybe closures), lowered and type-inferred as Bench is, interpreted by kit/interp (the oracle), emitted to JS and later wasm; Bench stays the GPU-able check, and a function using a CPU-only feature is CPU-only with its reason reported. Settle: which features enter the CPU tier and why; how a lambda's tier is decided (inferred vs declared); how the tiers call each other (a CPU function calling a Bench helper, never the reverse); memory management in wasm (arena per step? refcount? none and copy?); determinism and replay; how it reaches a run (runtime step written in the CPU tier vs Kernel slots); what retires (does trusted runtime JS stay?). Use Manuel's Typed as precedent (project/2026-11-25-manuel-ir-workbench/summary.md): ideas, no code. Test the design against at least three sketches' algorithms (Knuth-Plass, a PEG parser, Levenberg-Marquardt). Out of scope: building it.

data.title: kit/run: a rebuild that changes an extent leaves fit edges, Dialect edges and the page box stale

So after a rebuild that changes an extent (a param read at build time that resizes a level), a "fit" edge, a Dialect's edges(record) and the page box keep the old numbers. data.note:
Fixes the tier-0 review: a length's type follows its list's max, and a const copy of a checked read lowers again

- An f32 Dialect typed every list's length f32, so a UI, port or Draw
  lambda reading an open state list's length (max OPEN_MAX) made a Kernel
  the verifier refuses (V002), and an f32 counter was accepted against a
  length past 2^24. A length is now the Dialect's number type when that
  type holds the max exactly, else f64 (holdsLength in kit/ir/types.js,
  shared with the verifier), and a length bounds a loop only within the
  counter's exact range (L007). As the integrator ruled (note on o2RhFb),
  an f32 lambda reading a short list's length now computes in f32.
- Binding `const k = m` lifted the narrowing a real check earned on m, so
  a copy of a checked loop read was L008 (a DMG regression). A const copy
  of a presumed const is presumed too; a let copy takes the present type.
  `const [a] = [xs[i]]; if (a != null)` stays L003, documented.
- L003 says which list is exactly and which at most n when the difference
  sits in a record field, instead of printing two identical types.
- The docs that overclaimed are corrected in place; the verifier's
  loop-index rule gets direct tests in kit/ir.

data.title: kit/define: callSite gives a data: URL's calls no site when it holds parentheses
data.description: From controls-build-58 (FhnOhO), recorded as a gotcha; fix at the source instead. kit/define's callSite (site.js) reads a stack frame's URL with a pattern that stops at ( and ), which encodeURIComponent leaves unescaped, so a Program imported from a data: URL built that way has every call at one place and siteOf finds one place for all (H011). Fix the pattern to read the whole URL (a data: URL up to the :line:col suffix), with a test, then delete the gotcha from project/gotchas.md.

data.title: Decide: a Ref id's #n counts across an instance's slots, so each-built addresses are easy to get wrong
data.description: From controls-build-58 (FhnOhO). A Ref id's #<n> counts an instance's calls across all its slots in declaration order (g("s").param(...).op("a", ...) makes the op s.op#1), so an each lambda that builds an arg address from a list index (the controls draft's own pick example) addresses the wrong call whenever an earlier slot has calls. The draft is corrected in place. Decide whether addresses should count per slot (s.op#0), which every author would guess, at the cost of changing kit/define's Ref ids (and every record's ids and goldens), or stay as they are with a helper that gives the address of a slot's nth call.

data.title: Decide: a demand-only run never steps when played; let outside inputs make instants?
data.description:
From the tests rerun (aWrZQr; project/2026-11-27-tests-rerun-findings.md, "The demand clock"). Both blind game legs wrote clock: { demand: true }, the natural clock for a game steered by a person; run alone (a package's tests, a part played alone on the page) it never steps after T = 0: neither a test's in records nor the page's Control records make an instant, and nothing says why (11 H006 and a T010 each). kit/run's "Not here" lists "a workbench of demand parts only (nothing makes an instant)" as a conscious exclusion, but kit/package's README and kit/run's own line 83 promise a step "when an Event is ready".
Options: (a) an outside input (in, control, pointer) makes an instant at its stamp for the demand parts it reaches, so a demand-only run steps when played (recommended: a synth, a lens bench and a game are all demand-shaped); (b) keep the exclusion and warn at createRun (an N warning: every stepping part is demand, so only the first instant runs) and correct both READMEs. The integrator adds (b)'s warning now either way, since a silent no-op breaks "nothing is silent"; (a) is Ben's call because it moves a documented boundary of kit/run.

Both game legs guessed the buttons shape from U017's text in codes.js. data.text: Fixed (ctlfix-66). siteOf now returns the call's `slot` and its `source`: the value the text held when the record was built (the value before an override, for a preview's record built with run({ args }) or callGlue's args; kit/define records what applyArgs replaced, by Program then by record, in sites.js's REPLACED). writeback.js's locate refuses H012 when no call is at the place, when the call there is another method than the slot, or when the literal there is not site.source (deep-equal over numbers, strings, booleans and number lists). Test 46's H012 case (editSource directly) is replaced by a writeBack one: an edited literal, a line removed above, another method at the place, a nested literal and a param literal are H012; the original text, a preview's record and a list preview still write. Probe writeback-stale.probe.js passes. New: kit/define/test/arg-overrides.test.js "16. siteOf names the call's slot …".

Fixed (ctlfix-66). kit/compose's analyze links the part records of one composed record (kit/define/sites.js's BUILT_WITH), and siteOf counts the calls at a place across them, so a glue helper that makes two parts gives calls: 2 and write-back (and the page's Grip/Control check) is H011 "runs 2 times". Test: kit/page/test/writeback.test.js "45. a glue helper that makes two parts …" (lens bench, from a glue text; a glue whose parts each have their own call still writes). Probe glue-helper.probe.js passes. New fixture kit/page/fixtures/lens-program.js.

Fixed (ctlfix-66). kit/page/page.js logs every page input (key, pointer, blur's releases and cancels, Grip previews) through one logInput: the device time when the event has one, else the first ms after T, and never before the latest stamp the page logged (kit/run keeps one stamp's inputs in log order). stampOf also clamps a device time to the furthest the following frame can reach (the catch-up cap past the last frame, floored to the ms). Tests: kit/page/test/stamp.test.js, two "38." cases from the probe (blur after a stamped press; a 400 ms late press across a capped frame), each also checking what still maps. Probe stamp-order.probe.js passes. The rule is in kit/page/README.md (stampOf row, and the Invariants entry "Page inputs are logged in the order the page makes them", with a dated correction).

Fixed (ctlfix-66). kit/define/sites.js boundsAt: a path that ends on a list (of numbers, or lists of them) takes its element's bounds, so siteOf gives min/max per component and a translate Grip clamps each coordinate. kit/page/page.js: one preview(part, to, value) for Grips (and, now, Controls with to): a build that gives no record or throws is skipped, reported once as H012 (until one builds), and the release gives the last value that built; the frame loop no longer halts (H004). Tests: kit/page/test/grips.test.js "40b. a list of numbers takes its element's bounds…" and "40c. a preview whose build fails is skipped…" (lens bench from a Program text). Probe lens-bench.probe.js test 3 passes. README: H012 row and the grab row.

Fixed (ctlfix-66). kit/page/pointer.js edgeInto walks down from the shown layer through layer wires only, composing edges on the way, so an output that also feeds an unshown layer (declared first) is not mapped through it; a shown plain part gives null. Test: kit/page/test/pointer.test.js "39. a point maps only through the shown layer's path…" (both declaration orders, hits and the delivered down). Probe edge-layer.probe.js passes.

Fixed (ctlfix-66) by the first option: kit/define/ui/controls.js U017 refuses keys, gamepad and midi on a Control with each, and on an each entry (at lower), since a device record carries no key. Test: kit/define/test/ui-controls.test.js "4. U017: a keyed Control (each) takes no device binding…" (synth knob; an unkeyed knob keeps keys and MIDI, a keyed one on screen builds). Probe synth-page.probe.js test 2 passes (refused at defineUI). codes.js U017 text and kit/define/README.md updated.

Fixed (ctlfix-66). kit/run/delivery.js: a pointer move removes the earlier move of the same pointer id from the trailing run of moves and is pushed last, so each pointer keeps its last move and the queue stays in stamp order. Test: kit/run/test/pointer.test.js "30. moves coalesce per pointer…" (with a replay). Probe multitouch.probe.js passes. kit/run/README.md has a dated correction.

Fixed (ctlfix-66). kit/page/writeback.js editSource refuses spans that overlap (sorted, any span ending past the next one's start) as H011 with overlap: true, before writing anything; runAction turns that into H013 (the action gave two values for one place) and keeps nothing. Tests: kit/page/test/writeback.test.js "46. edits that overlap are refused…" (one target twice, a list and a point in it, editSource itself; adjacent and disjoint edits still apply) and an overlap case in actions.test.js 50. Probe overlap-edits.probe.js passes (refused).

Fixed (ctlfix-66). kit/page/page.js unlock() resumes the driver first, then calls each hook in a try/catch; a throw is H014 (a warning) and the other hooks run. Test: kit/page/test/controls.test.js "42. an unlock hook that throws…" (seen red against the old unlock, then green). Probe unlock-hook.probe.js passes. README: the lock row and H014.

Built (ctlfix-66). kit/page/page.js: page.controls() lists the wired page Controls in declaration order, then each part's part-local ones (local: true), each with part, to and disabled (its H011 or null) when it has a target, and a keyed Control's instances for the record in force (ui.compile(record).instances, newly exposed), each with its own to and disabled. New page.control(name, record, { phase?, timeStamp? }): a Control with an input logs the page input (stamped by the page's stamp rule) and carries the live value; with to, phase "preview" commits nothing and a part-local Control previews its target through the log at most once a frame (the shared preview(): a param input, or a rebuild built with the argument overridden; a failed build is H012); the release ("commit", the default) returns { part, to, value } for the host to write back. An unwritable target is H011 (listed once); a part-local Control's change then throws, one with an input still plays and returns null. Host: session.control goes through page.control (so it follows the stamp rule too) and hands a commit to a new onCommit option; session.forms() lists part-local Controls, keyed (not each) and instances; views.js controlForm shows one form per keyed instance, and a slider with to previews while it moves and commits on change; load.js gives a glue a rebuild that calls callGlue with args, so a glue part's argument previews. Not built (GR66N2, editor stage): the host passes no onCommit, so a commit is not written into the text. Keys, gamepad and MIDI play only wired Controls. Tests: kit/page/test/controls-to.test.js (synth: keyed knobs with to, a part-local param knob, an unwritable instance; lens: a part-local keyed radius over its lenses, the session's forms and onCommit), kit/page/host/test/views-controls.test.js, kit/page/host/test/load.test.js (glue rebuild). Probe: none (grep and read).

Fixed (ctlfix-66). (1) ctx.files on rebuild: delivering new files would change the rebuild input's (log) format, so not made; the limit is in kit/run/README.md's ctx table row (files read once at createRun; a host that swaps a package's data starts a new run). files-rebuild.probe.js still passes, showing the gap. (2) writeback.js literal() escapes \r; printNumber takes a step's decimals from its exponent form (1e-7 has seven). Test: writeback.test.js "46. a string with a carriage return …". literals.probe.js: the \r cases pass; its printNumber test still fails on its own expectations, 2.5e-8 to a step of 1e-8 wanting 2.5e-8 and 12.5 to a step of 5 wanting 10: half a step rounds up (Math.round, as gripValue's step does), giving 3e-8 and 15. (3) views.js controlForm checks form.keyed (session.forms gives it, from the composed Control's keyed) and shows one form per instance. Tests: kit/page/host/test/views-controls.test.js, controls-to.test.js "FtbfNP. a wired keyed Control's form …" (green on first run: the session change came with UYk5XG). keyed-form.probe.js still fails: it asserts form.each, the field the fix stopped reading. (4) kit/define/ui/lower.js controlInstances: an instance of a part-local keyed Control with no to (its own or the declaration's) is U017 at lower. Test: ui-controls.test.js "5. a part-local keyed Control …". (5) kit/page/host/README.md's examplePreset line now says wiring is by name; the dead #pad-* rule is gone from host.css.

Addendum (ctlfix-66): the latest stamp clears when the run's T goes back (a rewind starts a new branch), checked at each frame and each input; test stamp.test.js "38. after a rewind …" (seen red first).

The review of 787000e (reviewer-controls-64) found that write-back never
refused a stale text, that a glue helper's two parts shared one literal,

were not built at all. siteOf now gives the call's slot and the value its
text held (before any preview override), and counts calls across a
composition's records; write-back refuses with H012 a call that is not the

in the order it made them, never before the latest stamp (reset by a
rewind). page.control previews and commits Controls with `to`,
page.controls lists part-local and keyed instances, and the host's forms
and glue rebuild follow (the host passes no onCommit until the editor
stage, GR66N2). Also fixed: Grip list bounds and failed previews (skipped,
H012), pointer mapping through unshown layers, U017 for device bindings on
`each`, per-pointer move coalescing, overlapping edits, a throwing unlock
hook (H014), \r and exponent-step literals, the keyed form check, and
stale host docs and CSS. ctx.files on rebuild is documented as a limit,
since delivering new files would change the log format.

data.description: From reviewer-afe-72 (review of afe0cfc), probe local/rev-afe-72/a.probe.js. kit/page/page.js preview() (~line 222) skips the check when the page has no run.build and returns true, so pg.control("volume",{value:99}) on param.gain (max 2) commits 99 with no diagnostic; with a build it is H012. writeBack itself does no bounds check (d.probe.js writes NaN, Infinity, 99). The README row for control and the doc comment claim "a commit is only ever a value some build accepted". Fix: refuse as the arg path does, or check siteOf min/max and finiteness. data.title: Write-back: the identical-neighbor guard ignores object arguments' other keys
data.description: From reviewer-afe-72 (review of afe0cfc), probe local/rev-afe-72/e.probe.js. The guard against write-back moving onto an identical neighbor compares only literal top-level arguments: delete the first of two lenses both with radius: 10 and arg.b.lens#0:0.radius writes onto the survivor (its other keys, e.g. at, differ). Same for .k(3).k(3) reduced to .k(3). The README says such a call "is never overwritten", which overstates it; the 8XU2O2 test is green only because the name literal changed. data.text: Built option (a) in kit/run/scheduler.js (branch wt/instants-69, uncommitted). An in, pointer, page control (undelayed wire), param (not a param wire's) or rebuild input makes an instant at its stamp for the running demand part it reaches, but only while no tick or frame part runs. Beside a clocked part an input makes no instant, because S116 sizes a demand producer's queues by the clocked instants. A demand part also wakes when a param changed since its last commit (needed for the Grip preview). N014 is narrowed to a delayed wire or param wire into a demand part in a demand-only run. Open: carried-over delta records and delayed-wire records in a demand-only run wait for the next input; and should inputs make instants beside clocked parts too (that needs S116 to change)?

The mixed-run case is a separate decision.

data.title: Decide: should an outside input make instants beside a running clocked part (S116 queue sizing)?
data.description: From instants-69 (qsEYlW, 916b2fd), deviation 1. Ruling (a) is built for runs with no running clocked part. Beside a running tick or frame part, an outside input still makes no instant: its demand parts step at the clocked instants, because kit/compose's S116 sizes a demand producer's queue into a clocked consumer by counting the clocked instants; an instant per input would let a demand producer overrun the consumer's max (N002). Options: (a) keep as is (documented in kit/run README "Not built"); (b) inputs make instants in mixed runs too, with S116 re-sized (a kit/compose change). Recommended (a) until a workbench needs it: a demand part beside a clocked one already steps at that part's rate. Also open (documented): delta records past a step's max and records on a delayed wire wait for the next input in a demand-only run.

data.title: Run: an input stamped behind now in a demand-only run diverges on rewind
data.description: reviewer-76, probe local/rev-76/backstamp.probe.js (red). runUntil(2) with no input (lastT null), then run.input(in @ 0.5): accepted, nextInstant runs an instant at 1/2 while now is 2, and the checkpoint records {T: 1/2, now: 2}. After rewind(1) the live run stands at 2 and a fresh replay at 1, so the next unstamped input stamps differently. data.title: Write-back: the API writes a non-finite value, and its step option ignores bounds
data.description: From reviewer-80 (low, pre-existing). writeBack/writeBackAll as an API accept a non-finite value and write NaN or Infinity into the text (the rebuild then refuses it, B004); and their step option snaps from 0 with no bounds, unlike roundNumber's bounded snap. The page path is guarded (declaredProblem, builds, commits carry no step). Refuse a non-finite value with H012, and either take bounds with step or drop the option (no caller in the kit passes it).
